children.translated_text: The cause is non-dual, the conclusion that [the beloved] resembles dear ones, the sprinkling of nectar and the burning — even the fruit is contradictory in my heart.
Strikingness is <s>udāratā</s> (grandeur). // VKal_3,1.23 //

children.text: bandhasya vikaṭatvaṃ yadasāvudāratā / yasmin sati nṛtyantīva padānīti janasya varṇabhāvanā bhavati tadvikaṭatvam / līlāyamānatvamityarthaḥ / yathā ----
children.translated_text: The strikingness of the composition — that is <s>udāratā</s> (grandeur). When it is present, people feel as if the words are dancing — this is the impression [created]; 'strikingness' means gracefulness. For example —

children.text: svacaraṇaviniviṣṭairnūpurairnartakīnāṃ jhaṇiti raṇitamāsīt tatra citraṃ kalaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: The tinkling of anklets fastened to their own feet produced by the dancing girls was there, wondrous and melodious.
But not —
The tinkling of anklets attached to the lotus-feet of the dancing girls was charming, wondrous, and there.
Being the cause of clarity of meaning is <s>arthavyakti</s> (perspicuity of meaning). // VKal_3,1.24 //

children.text: yatra jhaṭityarthapratipattihetutvaṃ sa guṇo'rhavyaktiriti pūrvoktamudāharaṇam / pratyudāharaṇaṃ tu bhūyaḥ sulabhaṃ ca //24//
children.translated_text: Where there is the quality of being the cause of immediate apprehension of meaning — that quality is <s>arthavyakti</s> (perspicuity of meaning). The previously stated example [applies]. The counter-example, moreover, is easy to find. //24//
Brilliance is <s>kānti</s> (luster). // VKal_3,1.25 //

children.text: bandhasyojjvalatvaṃ nāma yadasau kāntiriti / yadabhāve purāṇacchāyetyucyate / yathā ----
children.translated_text: The brilliance of the composition — that is what is called <s>kānti</s> (luster). In its absence, [the composition] is said to have 'an old-fashioned coloring.' For example —
The vicinity of the forest-edge, clustered with the glances of doe-eyed women —
The contrary, however, is abundant and easy [to find]. And the verses here are —
The master poets declare the firmness of word-placement to be <s>ojas</s> (vigor);
governed by it, the verbal [compositions] are mostly a feast for the ears.
They declare <s>prasāda</s> (clarity) as looseness mixed with <s>ojas</s>;

children.text: anena na vinā satyaṃ svadate kāvyapaddhatiḥ //
children.translated_text: without it, the path of poetry does not truly delight.
Where many words take on the nature of being a single word,
with imperceptible junctures — that <s>śleṣa</s> (cohesion) is the supreme quality.
Adhering to a single pattern in each word and each verse,
[otherwise] difficult to compose and difficult to discern — <s>samatā</s> (evenness) is considered a quality.
That quality by which poetic efforts ascend and descend in sequence
is called <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) — by it <s>Sarasvatī</s> (the goddess of speech) is purified.
The separateness of words in composition is declared by the wise as <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness);
by it indeed, the arrangements of words flow freely like streams of honey.
Likewise, speech also, when strung together with all qualities by the wise —
the non-harshness of composition is called <s>saukumārya</s> (delicacy);
by this excellence, words are not rough or unfit for hearing.
The strikingness of composition is what they call <s>udāratā</s> (grandeur);

children.text: vaicitryaṃ na prapadyante yayā śūnyāḥ padakramāḥ //
children.translated_text: without which, word-sequences do not attain variety.
Where the movement of speech is as if following, while the content is as if leading —
because of being the cause of clarity of meaning, that quality is known as <s>arthavyakti</s> (perspicuity).

children.text:
aujjvalyaṃ kāntirityāhurguṇaṃ guṇaviśāradāḥ /
  purāṇavcitrasthānīyaṃ tena bandhyaṃ kavervacaḥ //
children.translated_text: Those skilled in qualities declare brilliance as the quality <s>kānti</s> (luster); by it, in place of an old-fashioned appearance, the poet's speech should be composed.
[These qualities] are not non-existent, because they are perceivable. // VKal_3,1.26 //
Indeed, these qualities are not non-existent, because they are perceivable. //26//
To [the objection that] even though perceivable by those who know them, they may be illusory, he says —
[They are] not illusory, because of the steadiness [of the perception]. // VKal_3,1.27 //
The qualities are not illusory, because the cognitive activity regarding them is steady. //27//
[They are] not properties of the word-arrangement, because [they are] not observed everywhere. // VKal_3,1.28 //

children.text: naite guṇāḥ pāṭhadharmāḥ / sarvatrādṛṣṭeḥ / yadi pāṭhadharmāḥ syustarhi viśeṣānapekṣāḥ santaḥ sarvatra dṛśyeran / na ca sarvatra dṛśyante / viśeṣāpekṣayā viśeṣāṇāṃ guṇatvād guṇābhyupagama eveti //28//
children.translated_text: These qualities are not properties of the word-arrangement. Because they are not observed everywhere. If they were properties of the word-arrangement, then, being independent of specific conditions, they should be observed everywhere. But they are not observed everywhere. Since qualities are qualities precisely because they depend on specific conditions, the acceptance of them as qualities [is confirmed]. //28//
Thus ends the first chapter of the third section on the discrimination of qualities, in the <s>Kāvyālaṅkārasūtravṛtti</s> composed by <s>Vāmana</s>. //3-1//

children.text: iti śrīkāvyālaṅkārasūtravṛttau guṇavivecane tṛtīye'dhikaraṇe prathamo'dhyāyaḥ guṇālaṅkāravivekaḥ , śabdaguṇavivekaśca //3-1//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first chapter of the third section on the discrimination of qualities in the <s>Śrī Kāvyālaṅkārasūtravṛtti</s>: the discrimination of qualities and ornaments, and the discrimination of verbal qualities. //3-1//
Now the second chapter of the third section.
Now, for the purpose of discriminating the qualities of meaning, he says —
Those same are the qualities of meaning. // VKal_3,2.1 //
Those same — <s>ojas</s> and the rest — are the qualities of meaning. //1//
The maturity of meaning is <s>ojas</s> (vigor). // VKal_3,2.2 //
The maturity, that is, the quality of ripeness, of the meaning — that is <s>ojas</s> (vigor).
A sentential expression for a word-meaning, and a word-designation for a sentence-meaning,
expansion and compression, and also purposefulness —
A sentential expression for a word-meaning, as in (<s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 2.75) —
'Then the light born from the eye, like the sky, of that [sage]' —
'the light born from the eye, of that [sage]'

children.text: iti vākyaṃ prayuktam / padasamūhaśca vākyamabhipretam / anayā diśānyadapi draṣṭavyam / tadyathā ----
children.translated_text: — a sentence has been employed. And by 'sentence,' a collection of words is meant. By this indication, other [examples] too should be examined. That is, for instance —
here, for the meaning expressible by the single word 'moon,'

children.text:
puraḥ pāṇḍucchāyaṃ tadanu kapilimnā kṛtapadaṃ
  tataḥ pākotsekādaruṇaguṇasaṃsargitavapuḥ /
  śanaiḥ śoṣārambhe sthapuṭanijaviṣkambhaviṣamaṃ
  vane vītāmo badaramarasatvaṃ kalayati //
children.translated_text: At first pale-hued, then marked with tawny traces, then with the body tinged with reddish streaks from the surge of ripening, gradually at the onset of drying, uneven with the spreading of its own natural girth — in the forest we observe the jujube fruit attaining its essence.

children.text: nacaivamatiprasaṅgaḥ / kāvyaśobhākaratvasya / guṇasāmānyalakṣaṇasyāvasthitatvāt / vākyārthe padābhidhānanṃ yathā ----
children.translated_text: And there is no excessive extension here, because the general definition of being productive of poetic beauty is maintained. A word-designation for a sentence-meaning, as follows —

children.text: divyeyaṃ na bhavati kiṃ tu mānuṣī
children.translated_text: 'This one is divine, is she not? No, rather she is human' —
'She blinks' —

children.text: ityāheti / asya vākyārthasya vyāsasamāsau / vyāso yathā ----
children.translated_text: thus it is stated. Expansion and compression of this sentence-meaning: Expansion, as follows —
what should be said [in this many words] is [expressed as:]

children.text:
ayaṃ nānākāro bhavati sukhaduḥkhavyatikaraḥ
  sukhaṃ vā duḥkhaṃ vā na bhavati bhavatyeva ca tataḥ /
  punastasmādūrdhvaṃ bhavati sukhaduḥkhaṃ kimapi tat
  punastasmādūrdhvaṃ bhavati na ca duḥkhaṃ , na ca sukham //
children.translated_text: This experience of mixed pleasure and pain takes many forms — sometimes there is pleasure, sometimes pain, and then it arises again; then beyond that, there is some [state] of pleasure and pain; then beyond that, there is neither pain nor pleasure.
Compression, as in (<s>Kumārasaṃbhava</s> 6.94) —
'This <s>Candragupta</s>-like prince, radiant as the moon, a youth,
has become a king, a refuge of the wise — fortunately, his efforts have borne fruit.'
'A refuge of the wise' —

children.text: ityasya ca subandhuṃ sācivyopakṣepaparatvāt sābhiprāyatvam / etena
children.translated_text: and since this implies the suggestion of <s>Subandhu</s>'s appointment as minister, it has purposefulness. By this,
'upon the tresses whose binding was loosened by passion, of <s>Sukeśī</s>' —
'of <s>Sukeśī</s>' —
the purposefulness of this [word] too is explained. //2//
here,
The purity of meaning is <s>prasāda</s> (clarity). // VKal_3,2.3 //
The purity of meaning — the inclusion of only what is necessary — is <s>prasāda</s> (clarity). For example —
The maiden <s>Sarvaṇā</s>, endowed with the grace of beauty and the onset of youth —
The contrary, however —
'Let my hand be served — this is a seat of spotless jeweled girdle' —
'a seat of girdle' —
since the hip region is already indicated by this alone, the qualifier is unnecessary. //3//
Coherence is <s>śleṣa</s> (cohesion). // VKal_3,2.4 //
Coherence is the fitting together of sequential ingenuity, unobtrusiveness, and logical consistency. That is <s>śleṣa</s> (cohesion). For example (<s>Amaruśataka</s> 16) —

children.text:
dṛṣṭvaikāsanasaṅgate priyatame paścādupetyādarā-
  dekasyā nayane nimīlya vihitakrīḍāsubandhacchalaḥ /
  īpadvakritakandharaḥ sapulakaḥ premollasanmānasā-
  mantarhāsalasatkapolaphalakāṃ dhūrto'parāṃ cumbati //
children.translated_text: Seeing his beloved seated on the same seat [with another], approaching from behind with affection, under the pretext of a playful binding [of eyes], he closed the eyes of one; then, with neck slightly turned, with horripilation, his mind surging with love, the rogue kissed the other, whose cheek-surface was languid with inner laughter.
In the compositions of <s>Śūdraka</s> and others, the elaboration of this [quality] is abundantly seen. //4//
Evenness is <s>samatā</s> (uniformity). // VKal_3,2.5 //

children.text: avaipamyaṃ prakramābhedaḥ samatā / kvacit kramo'pi bhidyate / yathā ----
children.translated_text: Evenness — the non-violation of sequence — is <s>samatā</s> (uniformity). Sometimes, however, the sequence is also violated. For example —

children.text:
cyutasumanasaḥ kundāḥ puṣpodgameṣvalasā drumā
  malayamarutaḥ sarpantīme viyuktadhṛticchidaḥ /
  atha ca savituḥ śītollāsaṃ lunanti marīcayo
  na ca jaraṭhatāmālambante klamodayadāyinīm //
children.translated_text: The <s>kunda</s> flowers have shed their blossoms, the trees are sluggish in putting forth flowers, these <s>Malaya</s> breezes creep forth, severing the composure of those separated [from their lovers]; and the rays of the sun strip away the delight of coolness, but do not assume the harshness that produces weariness.

children.text: ṛtusandhipratipādanapare'tra dvitīye pāde kramabhedo , malayamarutāmasādhāraṇatvāt / evaṃ dvitīyaḥ pādaḥ paṭhitavyaḥ ----
children.translated_text: In this [verse], which aims to describe the juncture of seasons, there is a violation of sequence in the second quarter, since the <s>Malaya</s> breezes are not specific [to this season]. The second quarter should be read thus —

children.text: manasi ca giraṃ vadhvantīme kiranti na kokilāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'And these cuckoos do not pour their calls, which penetrate the minds of brides.'
Thus. //5//

children.text: sugamatvaṃ vā'vaiṣamyamiti // VKal_3,2.6 [k: not in sutra] //
children.translated_text: Or, ease of comprehension is evenness. // VKal_3,2.6 //
The meaning is: what is easily gone through, that is, easily understood. For example (<s>Kumārasaṃbhava</s> 1.1) —
'In the northern direction there stands a divine mountain...'
and so forth.
Or, for example —
'Who is this veiled one, whose bodily charm is not fully manifest,
among the ascetics, like a new shoot among pale leaves?'
A counter-example is easy to find. //6//
The vision of meaning is <s>samādhi</s> (concentration). // VKal_3,2.7 //
'For an attentive mind sees meanings' —
this has been stated earlier (1-3-17v). //7//
The seeing, that is, the perception of meaning — because it causes concentration, it is [called] <s>samādhi</s>.
Meaning is of two kinds: non-derivative, or derived from the shade of another [work]. // VKal_3,2.8 //

children.text: yasyārthasya darśanaṃ samādhiḥ so'rtho dvividhaḥ ---- ayoniranyacchāyāyonirveti / ayonirakāraṇaḥ / avadhānamātrakāraṇa ityarthaḥ / anyasya kāvyasya chāyānyacchāyā tadyonirvā / tadyathā ----
children.translated_text: That meaning whose perception constitutes <s>samādhi</s> is of two kinds: non-derivative or derived from the shade of another [work]. 'Non-derivative' means without [external] cause — meaning that mere attention is the [sole] cause. 'The shade of another' means the suggestion of another literary work; 'derived from that' means having that as its source. For instance —

children.text:
mā bhaiḥ śaśāṅka mama śīdhuni nāsti rāhuḥ
  khe rohiṇī vasati kātara kiṃ vimeṣi /
  prāyo vidagdhavanitānavasaṅgameṣu
  puṃsāṃ manaḥ pracalatīti kimatra citram //
children.translated_text: 'Fear not, O moon, in my liquor there is no <s>Rāhu</s>; <s>Rohiṇī</s> dwells in the sky — O timid one, why do you blink? It is well known that in the encounters of amorous clever women, the minds of men waver — what is surprising in this?'
The meaning of the first verse is non-derivative. That of the second is derived from suggestion. //8//
Meaning is manifest and subtle. // VKal_3,2.9 //

children.text: yasyārthasya darśanaṃ samādhiriti , sa dvedhā vyaktaḥ sūkṣmaśca / vyaktaḥ sphuṭa udāhṛta eva //9//
children.translated_text: That meaning whose perception constitutes <s>samādhi</s> is twofold: manifest and subtle. 'Manifest' means clear — it has already been illustrated. //9//
To explain 'subtle,' he says —
The subtle is either to be contemplated or to be savored. // VKal_3,2.10 //

children.text: sūkṣmo dvedhā bhavato ---- bhāvyo, vāsanīyaśca / śīghranirūpaṇāgamyo bhāvyaḥ / ekāgratāprakarṣagamyo vāsanīya iti / bhāvyo yathā ----
children.translated_text: The subtle is of two kinds: to be contemplated (<s>bhāvya</s>) and to be savored (<s>vāsanīya</s>). What cannot be grasped by quick examination is <s>bhāvya</s> (to be contemplated). What is accessible through the height of concentration is <s>vāsanīya</s> (to be savored). The contemplatable is, for example —

children.text:
anyonyasaṃvalitamāṃsaladantakānti
  sollāsamāviralasaṃvalitārdhatāram /
  līlāgṛhe pratikalaṃ kilikiñciteṣu
  vyāvartamānanayanaṃ mithunaṃ cakrāsti //
children.translated_text:
With the radiance of teeth and flesh intertwined with each other,
with open delight, thick, entwined, in half-tones;
in the pleasure-house, at every moment, amid the <s>kilikiñcita</s> (mixed emotions),
the couple delighted, with eyes rolling about.
The <s>vāsanīya</s> (suggestive) [type], as follows —
Standing with her lower garment drawn aside without concealment, with her breast-slopes turned to face [him],
I was looked at by her, with a garland-string held in her right hand.
Variety of expression is <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness). // VKal_3,2.11 [*VKal_3,2.10] //
The variety that belongs to expression — that is <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness). As follows —

children.text:
rasavadamṛtaṃ , kaḥ sandeho madhūnyapi nānyathā
  madhuramadhikaṃ cūtasyāpi prasannarasaṃ phalam /
  sakṛdapi punarmadhyasthaḥ san rasāntaravijjano
  vadatu yadihānyat svādu syāt priyādaśanacchadāt //
children.translated_text:
Nectar is flavorful — who doubts it? — honey too is not otherwise;
even the fruit of the mango, with its clear juice, is exceedingly sweet.
But let an impartial person, learned in the varieties of flavor, speak even once:
what else here could be sweeter than the lip of the beloved?
The absence of harshness is <s>saukumārya</s> (delicacy). // VKal_3,2.12 [*VKal_3,2.11] //

children.text: puruṣe'rthe apāruṣyaṃ saukumāryamiti / yathā mṛtaṃ , yaśaḥśeṣamityāhuḥ / ekākinaṃ devatādvitīyamiti / gacchati sādhayeti ca //12//
children.translated_text: Non-harshness in harsh subjects is <s>saukumārya</s> (delicacy). For example: [instead of saying] 'he died,' [one says] 'he has become one whose fame alone remains'; [instead of] 'alone,' 'with a deity as companion'; and 'he goes' [meaning] 'he accomplishes.' //12//
The absence of vulgarity is <s>udāratā</s> (nobility). // VKal_3,2.13 [*VKal_3,2.12] //
Where there is occasion for vulgarity, the absence of vulgarity is <s>udāratā</s> (nobility). As follows —

children.text:
tvamevaṃ saundaryā sa ca ruciratāyāṃ paricitaḥ
  kalānāṃ sīmānaṃ parimiha yuvāmeva bhajathaḥ /
  ayi dvandvaṃ diṣṭyā taditi subhage saṃvadati vā-
  mataḥ śeṣaṃ cet syājjittamiha tadānīṃ guṇitayā //

children.translated_text: The opposite [i.e., vulgar] —

children.text: svapiti yāvadayaṃ nikaṭe janaḥ svapimi tāvadahaṃ kimapaiti te /
children.translated_text: While this person nearby sleeps, I too shall sleep — what does it mean to you?

children.text: iti nigadya śanairanumekhalaṃ mama karaṃ svakareṇa rurodha sā //
children.translated_text: Having said this softly, she restrained my hand with her own hand, near the girdle.
The clear manifestation of the nature of things is <s>arthavyakti</s> (clarity of meaning). // VKal_3,2.14 [*VKal_3,2.13] //

children.text: vastūnāṃ bhāvānāṃ svabhāvasya sphuṭatvaṃ yadasāvarthavyaktiḥ / yathā ----
children.translated_text: The clarity of the nature of things and emotions — that is <s>arthavyakti</s> (clarity of meaning). As follows —
On the backs of the eaves, which have the hue of conch-shell fragments, marked by stripes of lac and vermilion,
the water-lily in the pool delights, tinged yellow-brown by <s>gorocanā</s> (yellow orpiment) on its outer petals.
Or as follows —

children.text:
prathamamalasaiḥ paryastāgraṃ sthitaṃ pṛthukesarai-
  rviralaviralairantaḥpatrairmanāṅmilitaṃ tataḥ /
  tadanu valanāmātraṃ kiñcid vyadhāyi vahirdalai-
  rmukulanavidhau vṛddhābjānāṃ babhūva kadarthanā //
children.translated_text:
First standing with drooping tips and broad filaments that are languid,
then slightly closed with sparse inner petals;
then making only a slight bending with the outer petals —
in the process of closing, the full-blown lotuses were brought to naught.
<s>Kānti</s> (charm) is the brilliance of <s>rasas</s> (aesthetic sentiments). // VKal_3,2.15 [*VKal_3,2.14] //

children.text: dīptā rasāḥ śṛṅgārādayo yasya sa dīptarasaḥ / tasya bhāvo dīpta rasatvaṃ kāntiḥ / yathā ----
children.translated_text: That in which the <s>rasas</s> such as <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic) and others are brilliant is <s>dīptarasa</s> (brilliant in sentiment). Its quality — the brilliance of sentiments — is <s>kānti</s> (charm). As follows —

children.text:
preyān sāyamapākṛtaḥ saśapathaṃ pādānataḥ kāntayā
  dvitrāṇyeva padāni vāsabhavanāt yāvanna yātyūnmanāḥ /
  tāvat pratyuta pāṇisampuṭalasagnīvīnitambaṃ dhṛto
  dhāvitvaiva kṛtapraṇāmakamaho premṇo vicitrā gatiḥ //
children.translated_text:
The beloved, dismissed at evening with an oath by his mistress who bowed at his feet;
before he has gone even two or three steps from the dwelling, high-spirited,
he is rather seized by her, who runs after him and holds his waist with cupped hands —
alas, how wondrous is the way of love!
Thus it should be illustrated for the other <s>rasas</s> as well. Here are verses —
They call the maturity of poetry the clarity and completeness of <s>guṇas</s> (qualities);
and it is compared to the ripening of the mango.
That poetry which has correct nominal and verbal forms as its essence but forced qualities of content
is like the ripening of an eggplant — people loathe it.

children.text:
guṇānāṃ daśatāmukto yasyārthastadapārthakam /
  dāḍimāni daśetyādi na vicārakṣamaṃ vacaḥ //
children.translated_text:
That whose meaning is devoid of the ten-fold nature of qualities is purposeless;
the statement 'there are ten pomegranates' is not worthy of examination.
//15// Thus ends [the section]. //
Thus ends the second chapter of the third section on the discrimination of <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) in the commentary on the <s>Kāvyālaṅkāra-sūtras</s> composed by the eminent scholar <s>Vāmana</s>.
This third section on the discrimination of <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) is complete.
Now, the first chapter of the fourth section.

children.text: guṇanirvartyā kāvyaśobhā / tasyāścātiśayahetavo'laṅkārāḥ / tannirūpaṇārthamālaṅkārikamadhikaraṇamārabhyate / tatra śabdālaṅkārāḥ / tatra śabdālaṅkārau dvau yamakānuprāsau krameṇa darśayitumāha ----
children.translated_text: The beauty of poetry is effected by <s>guṇas</s> (qualities). And <s>alaṅkāras</s> (ornaments) are the causes of its enhancement. For their determination, the section on <s>alaṅkāras</s> is begun. Among them, [first] the <s>śabdālaṅkāras</s> (sound-figures). Of these, the two sound-figures — <s>yamaka</s> (rhyming repetition) and <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration) — to show them in order, he says —
A word of more than one meaning, or a syllable, repeated at fixed positions, is <s>yamaka</s> (rhyming repetition). // VKal_4,1.1 //

children.text: padamenekārthaṃ bhinnārthamekamanekaṃ vā tadvadakṣaranāvṛttaṃ sthānaniyame sati yamakam / svavṛttyā sajātīyena vā kārtsnyaikadeśābhyāmanekapādavyāptiḥ sthānaniyama iti / yāni tvekapādabhāgavṛttīni yamakāni dṛśyante teṣu ślokāntarasthasaṃsthānayamakāpekṣayaiva sthānaniyama iti //1//
children.translated_text: A word — of different meaning, one or many, or syllables resembling it — repeated at fixed positions is <s>yamaka</s>. The fixed position means occurrence across multiple verse-quarters by the whole or by a part, with its own repetition or with one of the same class. And those <s>yamakas</s> that occur in a portion of a single quarter have their fixed position in relation to the <s>yamaka</s> in another quarter of the verse. //1//
For the purpose of stating the positions, he says —
The quarters, and the beginning, middle, and end portions of one quarter and of multiple quarters, are the positions. // VKal_4,1.2 //

children.text: pādaḥ , ekasya ca pādasyādimadhyāntabhāgāḥ , anekasya ca pādasya ta eva sthānāni / pādayamakaṃ yathā ----
children.translated_text: A quarter, and the beginning, middle, and end portions of a single quarter, and the same of multiple quarters — these are the positions. Quarter-<s>yamaka</s>, as follows —
The speech of the wicked, condemned by the <s>kalikā</s> honey [of good poets],
of that tree of poison, is condemned by the <s>kalikā</s> honey.
Single-quarter beginning-, middle-, and end-<s>yamaka</s>, as follows —
Strike, O striker of enemies! O hero, your heroism is worshipped;
indeed, the policy of <s>Kāmandaka</s> [Kāmandakī-nīti] should be savored day and night.
In [women] whose wealth has departed, while giving up their very lives without flaw, with the radiance of the spotless moon,

children.text: priyatamaṃ yatamantumanīśvaraṃ rasikatā sikatāsviva tāsu kā //
children.translated_text: what passion is there among them for the most beloved, the controlled lord, as for sand on a river-bank?

children.text:
sudṛśo rasarecakitaṃ cakitaṃ bhavatīkṣitamasti mitaṃ stimitam /
  api hāsalavastavakastava kastulayennanu kāmadhurāṃ madhurām //
children.translated_text:
Of the beautiful one, the sentiment's playful tremor, the trembling — her glance is measured, is motionless;
and the cluster of her slight smile — your cluster — who could weigh the sweet intoxication of love?
Two-quarter beginning-, middle-, and end-<s>yamaka</s>, as follows —

children.text: bhramara ! drutapuṣpāṇi bhrama ratyau pivan madhu /
children.translated_text: O bee! Fly swiftly to the flowers, drinking honey in the season of love!

children.text: kā kundakusume prītiḥ kākuṃ dattvā virauṣi yat //
children.translated_text: What joy is there in the <s>kunda</s> (jasmine) blossom? Why do you buzz, making only plaintive cries?

children.text:
aṣyaśakyaṃ tayā dattaṃ duḥkhaṃ śakyantarātmani /
  vāṣyo vāhīkanārīṇāṃ vegavāhī kapolayoḥ //
children.translated_text:
The suffering given by her, unbearable for another, was borne within the self;
the tears of <s>Vāhīka</s> women are swift rivers upon their cheeks.
Instantly, by your glance that initiates steps, by the one initiated into the truth of love [Smara], pure with a smile,

children.text: bhavati vata janaḥ sacittad=aho na khalu mṛṣā kuta eva cittadāho //
children.translated_text: a person indeed becomes possessed of thought — alas! Surely the burning of the heart is not false — whence could it be?
Alternate-quarter end-<s>yamaka</s>, as follows —
The ill-governance of that king terrifies beings;
for him, soon separated from the throne, there is [only] ill-governance.
Similarly, alternate-quarter beginning- and middle-<s>yamakas</s> are to be inferred. Full-quarter end-<s>yamaka</s>, as follows —
Seeing the slender one with charming play like the movement of raised and lowered brows,

children.text: manaḥ kimuttāmyasi cañcalāsyāṃ kṛtī smarājñaā yadi puṣkalāsyām //
children.translated_text:
with a face beautiful as the moon,
O mind, why do you labor? She is fickle. The conqueror, Love, has triumphed, if she is bountiful in face.

children.text: evaṃ samastapādādimadhyayamakāni vyākhyātavyāni / anye ca saṅkarajātibhedāḥ sudhiyotprekṣyāḥ / akṣarayamakaṃ tvekākṣaramanekākṣaraṃ ca / ekākṣaraṃ yathā ----
children.translated_text: Thus full-quarter beginning- and middle-<s>yamakas</s> are to be explained. Other mixed varieties are to be imagined by the intelligent. Syllable-<s>yamaka</s> may be of one syllable or many syllables. One-syllable, as follows —
With various gestures, the beloved's eyebrow, like an honored youth of the mind,
with a distinctive grace, carved the hearts of men.

children.text: evaṃ sthānāntarayoge'pi draṣṭavyaḥ / sajāntīyanairantaryādasya prakarṣo bhavati / sa cāyaṃ hariprabodhe dṛśyate / yathā ----
children.translated_text: Similarly, it should be observed in the conjunction of different positions. Its excellence comes from unbroken continuity with its own kind. And that is seen in <s>Hariprabodha</s>. As follows —
With various white forests, with <s>Nāga</s> [mountain] ridges, spread across the skies, submerging people,
with deer, hares, and [other] leaping creatures, with bonds of <s>Dhundhunā</s> [winds], beneficial to us, with sounds of self-breathing.
And by this garland of syllable-<s>yamaka</s>, the garland of word-<s>yamaka</s> is also explained. //2//
Excellence comes from <s>bhaṅga</s> (breaking). // VKal_4,1.3 //
A <s>yamaka</s> becomes excellent indeed through <s>bhaṅga</s> (breaking). //3//
<s>Śṛṅkhalā</s> (chain), <s>parivartaka</s> (reversal), and <s>cūrṇa</s> (pulverization) are the modes of breaking. // VKal_4,1.4 //

children.text: ete khalu śṛṅkhalādayo yamakabhaṅgānāṃ prakārā bhavanti //4//
children.translated_text: These — <s>śṛṅkhalā</s> and the rest — are indeed the varieties of <s>yamaka</s>-breaking. //4//
He explains them in order —
<s>Śṛṅkhalā</s> (chain) is the shifting of the division of syllables. // VKal_4,1.5 //

children.text: varṇānāṃ vicchedo varṇavicchedaḥ / tasya calanaṃ yat sā śṛṅkhalā / yathā ---- kālikāmadhuśabde kāmaśabdavicchede madhuśabdavicchede ca tasya calanam / li-ma-varṇayorvicchedāt //5//
children.translated_text: The division of syllables is <s>varṇaviccheda</s>; the shifting of that is <s>śṛṅkhalā</s> (chain). As follows — in the word <s>kālikāmadhu</s>, when the word <s>kāma</s> is separated and the word <s>madhu</s> is separated, there is a shifting of those — due to the separation of the syllables <s>li</s> and <s>ma</s>. //5//
<s>Parivartaka</s> (reversal) is the emergence of the true form when the conjunction is removed. // VKal_4,1.6 //

children.text: anyavarṇasaṃsargaḥ saṅgaḥ / tadvinivṛttau svarūpasyānyavarṇatiraskṛtasyāpattiḥ prāptiḥ parivartakaḥ / yathā ----
children.translated_text: The conjunction with another syllable is <s>saṅga</s>. When that is removed, the emergence — the appearance — of the true form hidden by the other syllable is <s>parivartaka</s> (reversal). As follows —
'<s>kalikāmadhu garhitam</s>' (condemned by the honey of the bud) —

children.text: ityatrārhitamiti padaṃ gakārasya vyañjanasya saṅgād garhitamityanyasya rūpamāpannam / tatra vyañjanasaṅge vinivṛtte svarūpamāpadyate ---- arhitamiti / anyavarṇasaṃkrameṇa bhinnarūpasya padasya tādrūpyavidhirayamiti tātparyārthaḥ / etenetarāvapi vyākhyātau //6//
children.translated_text: Here, the word <s>arhitam</s> (honored), due to the conjunction with the consonant <s>ga</s>, takes on the form of another word <s>garhitam</s> (condemned). When the conjunction with the consonant is removed, it reverts to its true form — <s>arhitam</s>. The purport is that this is the process of producing the true form of a word whose form has been altered by the transposition of another syllable. By this, the other two [types] are also explained. //6//
<s>Cūrṇa</s> (pulverization) is the loss of the true form through the breaking of a compound syllable. // VKal_4,1.7 //

children.text: piṇḍākṣarasya bhede sati padasya svarūpalopaścūrṇam / yathā ----
children.translated_text: When a compound syllable is broken, the loss of the word's true form is <s>cūrṇa</s> (pulverization). As follows —
The shifting of an unbroken arrangement of syllables is the pure <s>śṛṅkhalā</s> (chain);
by this type of breaking indeed comes the variety of <s>yamakas</s>.
That by which, abandoning the conjunction with another, like a dancer [leaving] the costume,
one ascends to the true form of the word — that is to be known as <s>parivartaka</s> (reversal).
By the breaking of a compound syllable, from the dependence on preceding and following words,
the loss of a word between two syllables — that breaking is called <s>cūrṇa</s> (pulverization).
Those <s>yamakas</s> that have not attained the <s>cūrṇa</s> breaking, standing in their own positions,
do not shine exceedingly, like curls [without ornament].
Where breaking would occur through the change of case-endings,
those expert in the excellence of <s>yamaka</s> do not desire that [to be called] <s>yamaka</s>.
When a word has predominantly ascended to the platform of <s>yamaka</s>,
one should not then devise an <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration) for it.

children.text:
vibhaktīnāṃ vibhaktatvaṃ saṃkhyāyāḥ kārakasya ca /
  āvṛttiḥ suptiṅantānāṃ mithaśca yamakādabhutam //
children.translated_text:
The distinctness of case-endings, of number, and of case-relations;
the repetition of nominal and verbal forms with each other — [these produce] a wondrous [effect] different from <s>yamaka</s>.
The rest — that which is of similar form — is <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration). // VKal_4,1.8 //

children.text: padamekārthamanekārtha ca sthānāniyataṃ tadvidhamakṣaraṃ ca śeṣaḥ / sarūpo'nyena prayuktena tulyarūpo'nuprāsaḥ / nanu śeṣo'nuprāsa ityetāvadeva sūtraṃ kasmānna kṛtam / āvṛttiśeṣo'nuprāsa ityeva hi vyākhyāsyate / satyam / siddhyatyevāvṛttiśeṣe , kintvavyāptiprasaṅgaḥ / viśeṣārtha ca sarūpagrahaṇam / kārtsnyenaivāvṛttiḥ / kārtsnyaikadeśābhyāṃ tu sārūpyamiti //8//
children.translated_text: A word of one meaning or many meanings, not fixed to particular positions, and syllables of that kind — this is the remainder. Having similar form — that is, identical in form with another [word or syllable] used [nearby] — is <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration). Now, why was the <s>sūtra</s> not simply made as 'the remainder is <s>anuprāsa</s>'? Indeed it will be explained as 'what remains from repetition is <s>anuprāsa</s>.' True. But [the fuller form] avoids under-extension. And the word <s>sarūpa</s> (similar form) is for specifying; for repetition is [only] in its entirety, but similarity may be in whole or in part. //8//
Unobtrusive syllable-<s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration) is better. // VKal_4,1.9 //

children.text: varṇānāmanuprāsaḥ sa khalvanulvaṇo līnaḥ śreyān / yathā ----
children.translated_text: Syllable-<s>anuprāsa</s> — that which is unobtrusive, subtle — is better. As follows —

children.text:
kvacinmasṛṇamāṃsalaṃ kvacidatīva tārāspadaṃ
  prasannasubhagaṃ muhuḥ svarataraṅgalīlāṅkitam /
  idaṃ hi tava vallakīraṇitanirgamairgumphitaṃ
  mano madayatīva me kimapi sādhu saṃgītakam //
children.translated_text:
Smooth and full here, exceedingly reaching high notes there,
clear and beautiful, constantly marked by the play of melodic waves —
this music of yours, woven from the outpourings of the <s>vallakī</s> (lute),
delights my mind with something beautifully good.
But obtrusive [alliteration] is not better. As follows —
<s>Vallībaddhordhvajūṭodbhaṭamaṭatiraṭatkoṭikodaṇḍadaṇḍaḥ</s>
— and so on. //9//
Quarter-<s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration) is like quarter-<s>yamaka</s>. // VKal_4,1.10 //

children.text: ye pādayamakasya bhedāste pādānuprāsasyetyarthaḥ / teṣāmudāharaṇāni yathā ----
children.translated_text: The varieties of quarter-<s>yamaka</s> are also those of quarter-<s>anuprāsa</s> — this is the meaning. Their examples, as follows —
Not knowing the king of poets, whence comes regard for poetic composition?
And knowing the king of poets, whence [then] comes regard for poetic composition?

They break the <s>āmalakī</s> fruits repeatedly;
the young ones, with eyes tawny as those of young monkeys.

children.text:
vastrāyante nadīnāṃ sitakusumadharāḥ śakrasaṅkāśa ! kāśāḥ
  kāśābhā bhānti tāsāṃ navatulinagatāḥ śrīnadīhaṃsa haṃsāḥ /
  sābhāmbhodamuktaḥ sphuradamalarucirmedinī candracandra-
  ścandrāṅkaḥ śāradaste jayakṛdupagato vidviṣāṃ kālakālaḥ //
children.translated_text:
The white-flowered <s>kāśa</s> grasses serve as garments for the rivers, O one resembling <s>Śakra</s> (Indra)!
The <s>haṃsas</s> (swans), resting upon the fresh lotuses, shine with the luster of <s>kāśa</s> — O swan of the <s>Śrī</s>-river!
The bright, spotless-rayed moon, released from the clouds — O moon, O moon of the earth!
The autumnal [season], bearing the mark of the moon, victorious, has arrived — the death of death for your enemies!

children.text:
kuvalayadalaśyāmā meghā vihāya divaṃ gatāḥ
  kuvalayadalaśyāmo nidrāṃ vimuñcati keśavaḥ /
  kuvalayadalaśyāmā śyāmā latādya vijṛmbhate
  kuvalayadalaśyāmaṃ candro nabhaḥ pratigāhate //

children.translated_text: Similarly, other [examples] should also be noted. //10//
Thus ends the first chapter of the fourth section, the <s>Ālaṅkārika</s> (on ornamentation), in the <s>Kāvyālaṅkārasūtravṛtti</s> composed by the eminent scholar <s>Vāmana</s>.
Thus concludes the discussion of verbal ornaments (<s>śabdālaṅkāra</s>).
Now, the second chapter of the fourth section.

children.text: sampratyarthālaṅkārāṇāṃ prastāvaḥ / tanmūlaṃ copameti saiva vicāryate ----
children.translated_text: Now begins the occasion for [discussing] figures of meaning (<s>arthālaṅkāras</s>). And since <s>upamā</s> (simile) is the root of these, that very [figure] is examined —
<s>Upamā</s> (simile) is the resemblance of the <s>upameya</s> (object of comparison) with the <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison) based on a partial quality. // VKal_4,2.1 //

children.text: upamīyate sādṛśyamānīyate yenotkṛṣṭaguṇenānyattadupamānam / yadupamīyate nyūnaguṇaṃ tadupameyam / upamānenopameyasya guṇaleśataḥ sāmyaṃ yadasāvupameti / nanūpamānamityupameyamiti ca sambandhiśabdāvetau , tayorekataropādānenaivānyatarasiddhiriti / yathā

children.translated_text: "the compared (upamita) is [implicitly known] with tigers and such, when there is no use of a generic [comparison]"

children.text: ityatropamitagrahaṇameva kṛtaṃ , nopamānagrahaṇamiti / tadvadatrobhayagrahaṇaṃ na kartavyam / satyam / tat kṛtaṃ lokaprasiddhiparigrahārtham / yadevopameyamupamānañca lokaprasiddhaṃ tadeva parigṛhyate , netarat / na hi yathā
children.translated_text: here, only the term 'compared' (upamita) is used, not 'standard of comparison' (upamāna). Similarly, both need not be mentioned here. True. But both are mentioned for the purpose of conforming to common understanding. Only what is well-known as <s>upameya</s> and <s>upamāna</s> in common usage is accepted, not otherwise. For it is not the case that just as
"the face is like a lotus"
[is a valid simile], so too
"like a night-lily"
would be [equally valid]. //1//

The <s>upamāna</s> is that which possesses superior qualities and by which comparison is made, i.e. resemblance is drawn. The <s>upameya</s> is that which is compared and possesses inferior qualities. The resemblance of the <s>upameya</s> with the <s>upamāna</s> based on a partial quality — that is <s>upamā</s> (simile). Now, since <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> are correlative terms, the establishment of one by the mention of the other [should suffice]. Just as in
And [there is simile] based on an abundance of qualities — the invented [type]. // VKal_4,2.2 //

children.text: guṇānāṃ bāhulyaṃ guṇabāhulyaṃ , tata upamānopameyayoḥ sāmyāt kalpitopamā / kavibhiḥ kalpitatvāt kalpitā / pūrvā tu laukikī / nanu kalpitāyā lokaprasiddhyabhāvāt kathamupamānopameyaniyamaḥ / guṇabāhukyasyotkarṣāpajarpakalpanābhyām / tadyathā ----
children.translated_text: An abundance of qualities — from that, due to the resemblance between the <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s>, there is the invented (<s>kalpitā</s>) simile. It is called 'invented' because it is devised by poets. The former [type] is the conventional (<s>laukikī</s>). Now, since the invented [simile] lacks common recognition, how is the restriction of <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> determined? Through the devices of exaggeration and deprecation based on an abundance of qualities. For example —
The disk of the moon, its surface rounded like the upthrust breasts of young <s>Hūṇa</s> women crushed in amorous sport,
with its foremost rays, pale as the sharp tips of stalks of poison, illuminates the first step of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
"An orange, rivaling the chin of a freshly shaven, intoxicated <s>Hūṇa</s> youth."
"A <s>śirīṣa</s> flower on the ear, rivaling the tip of a fresh <s>kuśa</s> blade."

children.text:
idānīṃ plakṣāṇāṃ jaraṭhadalaviśleṣacatura-
  stibhīnāmābaddhasphuritaśukacañcūpuṭanibham /
  tataḥ strīṇāṃ hanta kṣamamadharakāntiṃ tulayituṃ
  samantānniryāti sphuṭasubhagarāgaṃ kisalayam //
children.translated_text:
Now the sprout emerges on all sides, with beautiful, vivid color,
resembling the gaping crevices of aged, splitting fig-tree leaves —
apt indeed to match the beauty of women's lips;
already skilled in producing the quivering beaks of parrots.
Its twofold [division is] based on the distinction between word-meaning-function and sentence-meaning-function. // VKal_4,2.3 //

children.text: tasyā upamāyā dvaividhyam / padavākyārthavṛttibhedāt / ekā padārthavṛttiḥ , anyā vākyārthavṛttiriti / padārthavṛttiryathā ----
children.translated_text: That <s>upamā</s> is of two kinds, based on the distinction between word-meaning-function (<s>padārthavṛtti</s>) and sentence-meaning-function (<s>vākyārthavṛtti</s>). One operates at the level of word-meaning, the other at the level of sentence-meaning. At the word-meaning level, for example —

children.text:
haritatanuṣu babhrutvagvimuktāsu yāsāṃ
  kanakakaṇasadharmā mānmatho romabhedaḥ /
children.translated_text:
"On their green-skinned [bodies], having shed the tawny bark,
the erotic horripilation resembles grains of gold."
At the sentence-meaning level, for example —
"This <s>Pāṇḍya</s> king, with a long garland hanging over his shoulder, his body anointed with <s>haricandana</s> (yellow sandalwood),
shines like the king of mountains, its peak reddened by the morning sun, with cascading waterfalls."
It is <s>pūrṇā</s> (complete) and <s>luptā</s> (elliptical). // VKal_4,2.4 //

children.text: sā upamā pūrṇā luptā ca bhavati //4//
children.translated_text: That <s>upamā</s> (simile) is either complete or elliptical. //4//
When the words for quality, indicator, <s>upamāna</s>, and <s>upameya</s> are all present, it is <s>pūrṇā</s> (complete). // VKal_4,2.5 //
When there is completeness, i.e. totality, of the words for quality and the rest, it is <s>pūrṇā</s> (complete). For example —
"This face is charming like a lotus."
When [any of these is] omitted, it is <s>luptā</s> (elliptical). // VKal_4,2.6 //

children.text: guṇādiśabdānāṃ vaikalye lope luptā / guṇaśabdalope yathā

children.translated_text: "The king is like the moon."
With omission of the indicator-word, for example:
"She is <s>dūrvā</s>-grass-dark."
With omission of both, for example:
"Moon-faced."
The omission of <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> should be seen in the detailed treatment of <s>upamā</s>. //6//
When there is deficiency, i.e. omission, of the words for quality and the rest, it is <s>luptā</s> (elliptical). With omission of the quality-word, for example:
In praise, blame, and factual description. // VKal_4,2.7 //

children.text: stutau nindāyāṃ tattvākhyāne cāsyāḥ prayogaḥ / stutinindayoryathā
children.translated_text: Its use is in praise, in blame, and in factual description. In praise and blame, for example:

children.text:
snigdhaṃ bahvatyamṛtakalpamaho kalatraṃ
  hālāhalaṃ viṣamivāpaguṇaṃ tadeva /
children.translated_text:
"Ah, how loving and abundant is a wife, like nectar!
But that very same one, bereft of virtues, is like <s>hālāhala</s> (deadly poison)."
In factual description, for example —
"Know that one as <s>Rohiṇī</s> in this circle of luminaries,
O slender one, where the arrangement of stars has assumed the form of a cart."
Inferiority, excess, gender-discordance, number-discordance, dissimilarity, and impossibility are defects of that [simile]. // VKal_4,2.8 //

children.text: tasyā upamāyā doṣā bhavanti / hīnatvamadhikatvaṃ liṅgabhedo vacanabhedo'sādṛśyamasambhava iti //8//
children.translated_text: The defects of that <s>upamā</s> are: inferiority, excess, gender-discordance, number-discordance, dissimilarity, and impossibility. //8//
To explain these in order, he says —
The inferiority of the <s>upamāna</s> in class, measure, or quality is <s>hīnatva</s> (inferiority). // VKal_4,2.9 //

children.text: jātyā pramāṇena dharmeṇa copamānasya nyūnatā yā taddhīnatvamiti / jātinyūnatvarūpaṃ hīnatvaṃ yathā ----
children.translated_text: The inferiority of the <s>upamāna</s> in class, measure, or quality — that is <s>hīnatva</s>. Inferiority in the form of class-inferiority, for example —
"A supreme act of violence has been committed by you, as if by <s>Cāṇḍālas</s> (outcastes)."
Inferiority in the form of measure-inferiority, for example —
"This sun shines like a spark of fire."

children.text: upameyādupamānasya nyūnatvaṃ yat taddharmanyūnatvam / tadrūpaṃ hīnatvaṃ yathā ----
children.translated_text: The inferiority of the <s>upamāna</s> in qualities relative to the <s>upameya</s> is quality-inferiority. That form of inferiority, for example —
"That sage, marked with the <s>mauñjī</s> (muñja grass girdle), wearing a black antelope skin,
shone like the sun embracing the edge of a dark cloud."

children.text: atra mauñjīprativastu taḍinnāstyupamāna iti hīnatvam / na ca kṛṣṇājinapaṭamātrasyopameyatvaṃ yuktam / mauñjyā vyarthatvaprasaṅgāt / nanu nīlajīmūtagrahaṇenaiva taḍitpratipādyate / tanna / vyabhicārāt //9//
children.translated_text: Here, there is nothing in the <s>upamāna</s> corresponding to the <s>mauñjī</s> girdle, such as lightning — hence the inferiority. Nor is it proper to make only the antelope skin the <s>upameya</s>, for that would render the <s>mauñjī</s> girdle purposeless. Now, surely the mention of the dark cloud itself implies lightning? No, because of ambiguity. //9//

children.text: avyabhicāre tu bhavantī pratipattiḥ kena vāryate tadāha ----
children.translated_text: But when there is no ambiguity, who can prevent understanding? To this he says —
When one of two qualities is mentioned, the other is understood — because of their association. // VKal_4,2.10 //

children.text: dharmayorekasyāpi dharmasya nirdeśe'nyasya saṃvit pratipattirbhavati / kutaḥ / sāhacaryāt / sahacaritatvena prasiddhayoravaśyamekasya nirdeśe'nyasya pratipattirbhavati / tadyathā ----
children.translated_text: When even one quality is mentioned, the other is understood. Why? Because of their association. When two things are well-known as going together, the mention of one necessarily brings about the understanding of the other. For example —

children.text:
nirvṛṣṭe'pi bahirdhane na viramantyantarjaradceśmano
  lūtātantutaticchido madhupṛṣatpiṅgāḥ payovindavaḥ /
  cūḍābarbarake nipatya kaṇikābhāvena jātāḥ śiśo-
  raṅgāsphālanabhagnanidragṛhiṇīcittavyathādāyinaḥ //
children.translated_text:
"Even when the external rainfall has ceased, the old interior dripping does not stop;
the drops, breaking through the web of spider-threads, tawny as drops of honey,
falling into the matted topknot of the child, becoming tiny particles,
cause the heartache of the sleepy wife whose body is being tapped."

children.text: atra madhupṛṣatāṃ vṛttatvapiṅgatve sahacarite / tatra piṅgaśabdena piṅgatve pratipanne vṛttatvapratītirbhavati / etena

children.translated_text: "the image of the row [reflected] in a gold plate, rectangular"

children.text: iti vyākhyātam / kanakaphalakasya gauratvacaturasratvayoḥ sāhacaryāccaturasratvaśrutyaica gauratvapratipattiriti / nanu ca yadi dharmanyūnatvamupamānasya doṣaḥ , kathamayaṃ prayogaḥ ----
children.translated_text: is also explained. Since the yellowness and rectangularity of a gold plate are associated, from the mention of rectangularity, yellowness is also understood. Now, if quality-inferiority of the <s>upamāna</s> is a defect, how is this usage [possible] —
Here, the roundness and tawniness of honey-drops are associated. When tawniness is understood through the word 'tawny' (<s>piṅga</s>), roundness is also understood. By this,
"When the eyes were shut tight by the sun's rays, when the lotuses drooped in misery,

children.text: sādhvyaḥ svageheṣviva bhartṛhīnāḥ kekā vineśuḥ śikhināṃ mukheṣu //
children.translated_text: like virtuous wives in their own homes, bereft of their husbands, the cries of the peacocks vanished from their beaks."

children.text: atra bahutvamupameyadharmāṇāmupamānāt / na , viśiṣṭānāmeva mukhānāmupameyatvāt / tādṛśeṣveva kekāvināśasya sambhavāt //10//
children.translated_text: Here the <s>upameya</s>'s qualities are more numerous than the <s>upamāna</s>'s. No, because only the particular faces [of the peacocks] are the <s>upameya</s>, and the cessation of cries is possible only in such [faces]. //10//
By that [i.e. inferiority], excess is [also] explained. // VKal_4,2.11 //

children.text: tena hīnatvenādhikatvaṃ vyākhyātam / jātipramāṇadharmādhikyamadhikatvamiti / jātyādhikyarūpamadhikatvaṃ yathā ----
children.translated_text: By that [discussion of] inferiority, excess is also explained. Excess in class, measure, and quality constitutes <s>adhikatva</s> (excess). Excess in the form of class-excess, for example —

children.text: viśantu viṣṭayaḥ śīghraṃ rudrā iva mahaujasaḥ
children.translated_text: "Let the warriors enter swiftly, like the <s>Rudras</s> of great power!"
Excess in the form of measure-excess, for example —
"Your navel is like the netherworld, your breasts are like mountains,
and this braid-staff of yours resembles the descent of the <s>Kālindī</s> (Yamunā) river."
Excess in the form of quality-excess, for example —
"The lord, bearing the discus with its rays, restless and spinning, shone
like the leader of rivers, with the submarine fire and whirlpool."

children.text: savāḍavāgnirityasya [k:prativastunaḥ] upameye'bhāvād dharmādhikyamiti / anayordoṣayorviparyayākhyasya doṣasyāntarbhāvānna pṛthagupādānam / ata evāsmākaṃ mate ṣaḍ doṣā iti //11//
children.translated_text: Since the counterpart of 'with the submarine fire' has no presence in the <s>upameya</s>, it is quality-excess. Since the defect called 'reversal' (<s>viparyaya</s>) is subsumed under these two defects [inferiority and excess], it is not separately mentioned. Hence in our view, there are six defects. //11//
The transposition of gender between <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> is <s>liṅgabheda</s> (gender-discordance). // VKal_4,2.12 //

children.text: upamānasyopameyasya ca liṅgayorvyatyāso viparyayo liṅgabhedaḥ / yathā ----
children.translated_text: The transposition, i.e. reversal, of the genders of <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> is <s>liṅgabheda</s>. For example —
"The armies went forth unrestrained, like rivers."
It is generally acceptable between masculine and neuter. // VKal_4,2.13 //
"He gazes at the face like the moon"
[where <s>candra</s> (moon) is masculine and <s>mukha</s> (face) is neuter],
"the face shines like the moon (<s>indu</s>)"
— such [discordance] they do not find objectionable. //13//
Gender-discordance between masculine and neuter in the <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> is generally, i.e. mostly, acceptable. For example —
In conventional [similes], in compound-expressed [similes], and in elaborated similes. // VKal_4,2.14 //

children.text: laukikyāmupamāyāṃ samāsābhihitāyāmupamāyāmupamāprapañce ceṣṭo liṅgabhedaḥ prāyeṇeti / laukikyāṃ yathā ----
children.translated_text: In conventional similes, in compound-expressed similes, and in elaborated similes (<s>upamāprapañca</s>), gender-discordance is generally acceptable. In conventional [similes], for example —

children.text: chāyeva sa tasyāḥ , puruṣa iva strī
children.translated_text: "He is like her shadow; the woman is like a man."
In compound-expressed [similes], for example —
"The arm-creeper resembling a blue lotus."
In elaborated similes, for example —
"If this form, rare in the inner chambers, belongs to a forest-dwelling person,
then indeed the garden creepers have been surpassed in virtues by the forest creepers!"
Similarly, other examples of usage should also be noted. //14//
By that [gender-discordance], number-discordance is [also] explained. // VKal_4,2.15 //
By gender-discordance, number-discordance is also explained. For example —
"He will drink in her eye, like a bee [drinks] a flower."
<s>Asādṛśya</s> (dissimilarity) is resemblance based on unrecognized qualities. // VKal_4,2.16 //
Resemblance based on qualities that are not recognized — that is <s>asādṛśya</s> (dissimilarity). For example —
"I compose this poem-moon with widely spread rays of meaning."

children.text: kāvyasya śaśinā saha yat sādṛśyaṃ tadapratītaireva guṇairiti / nanu ca arthānāṃ raśmitulyatve sati kāvyasya śaśitulyatvaṃ bhaviṣyati / naivam / kāvyasya śaśitulyatve siddhe'rthānāṃ raśmitulyatvaṃ siddhyati / na hyarthānāṃ ca kaścit sādṛśyahetuḥ pratīto guṇo'sti / tadevamitaretarāśrayadoṣo duruttara iti //16//
children.translated_text: The resemblance of the poem to the moon is based on unrecognized qualities. Now, if the equivalence of meanings to rays is established, then the equivalence of the poem to the moon would follow. Not so — for when the equivalence of the poem to the moon is already assumed, then the equivalence of meanings to rays becomes established. For there is no recognized quality of meanings that serves as the basis of resemblance [to rays]. Thus the defect of mutual dependence (<s>itaretarāśraya</s>) is difficult to refute. //16//
For simile is ruined by dissimilarity, and poets are dependent on that [resemblance]. // VKal_4,2.17 //

children.text: asādṛśyena hatā asādṛśyahatā upamā / tanniṣṭhā upamānaniṣṭhāśca kavaya iti //17//
children.translated_text: <s>Upamā</s> ruined by dissimilarity is a <s>asādṛśya-hatā</s> (similarity-ruined) simile. And poets are dependent on the <s>upamāna</s>. //17//
Some say: through an abundance of <s>upamānas</s>, that [dissimilarity] is removed. // VKal_4,2.18 //
Some think that through an abundance of <s>upamānas</s>, that dissimilarity is removed. For example —
"Your fame is white like camphor, a garland, <s>Hara</s>'s (<s>Śiva</s>'s) laughter."

children.text: karpūrādibhirupamānairvahubhiḥ sādṛśyaṃ susthāpitaṃ bahvati / teṣāṃ śukguṇātirekāt //18//
children.translated_text: Through many <s>upamānas</s> such as camphor and the rest, the resemblance is well-established, since it is abundant. Because of the preponderance of the quality of whiteness in those [upamānas]. //18//
No, because the meaning is not strengthened [thereby]. // VKal_4,2.19 //

children.text: upamānādhikyāt tadapoha iti yuktaṃ , tanna / apuṣṭārthatvāt / ekasminnupamāne prayukte upamānāntaraprayogo na kañcidarthaviśeṣaṃ puṣṇāti / tena

children.translated_text: "The army-ocean, agitated like the ocean"

children.text: iti prayuktam / nanu sindhuśabdasya dviḥprayogātpaunaruktyam / na / arthaviśeṣāt balaṃ sindhuriva vaipulyād balasindhuḥ sindhuriva kṣubhita iti kṣobhasārūpyāt / tasmādarthabhedānna paunaruktyam / arthapuṣṭistu nāsti / sindhuriva kṣubhita ityanenaiva vaipulyaṃ pratipatsyate / uktaṃ hi (4-2-10) ----
children.translated_text: Thus it is used. Now, is there not redundancy because the word '<s>sindhu</s>' (ocean/river) is used twice? No, because of a difference in meaning: the army is like an ocean in vastness, hence '<s>balasindhu</s>' (army-ocean); and it is agitated like an ocean, hence the resemblance in agitation. Therefore, due to the difference in meaning, there is no redundancy. But there is no enrichment of meaning, since the vastness would be understood merely from 'agitated like an ocean.' For it has been said (4-2-10) —
'When one property is mentioned together, the other is known by association.'

That the dissimilarity is removed through an abundance of <s>upamānas</s> — that is not so. Because the meaning is not strengthened. When one <s>upamāna</s> has been employed, the use of another <s>upamāna</s> does not strengthen any particular additional meaning. Thus —
<s>Anupapatti</s> (impossibility) is the incongruity [of the simile]. // VKal_4,2.20 //
<s>Anupapatti</s> is the impossibility, i.e., the incongruity of the <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison). For example —
'Within the face, which blossoms with the gleam of a smile,
there shines, like innocent moonlight, in the center of a fully-opened lotus.'

The impossibility is that a lotus opens in the presence of moonlight [whereas in reality it closes]. Now, one might say this is a contradiction of meaning, not a fault of simile. No, because in simile, exaggeration is desirable. //20//
Then how is it a fault? To this he says —
Exaggeration that is self-contradictory [is a fault]. // VKal_4,2.21 //

children.text: viruddhasyātiśayasya saṃgraho na kartavya iti asya sūtrasya tātparyārthaḥ / tānetān ṣaḍupamādoṣān jñātvā kaviḥ parityajet //21//
children.translated_text: The purport of this <s>sūtra</s> is that self-contradictory exaggeration should not be employed. Having known these six faults of simile, a poet should avoid them. //21//
Thus ends the second chapter on the examination of simile, in the fourth section on figures of speech, in the <s>Kāvyālaṅkārasūtravṛtti</s>.
Now the third chapter in the fourth section.
Now the elaboration of simile is examined. What is that? He says —
The elaboration of simile consists of <s>prativastu</s> (counter-object) and what follows. // VKal_4,3.1 //

children.text: prativastu prabhṛtiryasya sa prativastuprabhṛtiḥ / upamāyāḥ prapañca upamāprapañca iti //1//
children.translated_text: That which begins with <s>prativastu</s> constitutes the elaboration of <s>upamā</s> (simile). //1//
To show the distinction between <s>prativastu</s> and <s>vākyārtho-pamā</s> (sentential simile), he says —
<s>Prativastu</s> (counter-object) is the placement of a parallel subject when the <s>upameya</s> (object of comparison) is explicitly stated. // VKal_4,3.2 //

children.text: upameyasyārthaādvākyārthasyoktau satyāmiti / atra dvau vākyārthau / eko vākyārthopamāyāmiti bhedaḥ / tadyathā ----
children.translated_text: 'When the <s>upameya</s>, i.e., the sentence-meaning, is stated' — here there are two sentence-meanings. In the case of <s>vākyārtho-pamā</s> there is one — that is the distinction. For example —
'Having been made a goddess, how can she assume the role of an attendant?
Surely a gem inscribed with a divine image is not fit for [ordinary] use.'
To show the distinction between <s>prativastu</s> and <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression), he says —
<s>Samāsokti</s> (condensed expression) is [the placement of a parallel subject] when [the upameya] is not stated. // VKal_4,3.3 //

children.text: upameyasyānuktau samānavastunyāsaḥ samāsoktiḥ / saṃkṣepavacanāt samāsoktirityākhyā / yathā ----
children.translated_text: When the <s>upameya</s> (object of comparison) is not stated, the placement of a parallel subject is <s>samāsokti</s>. It is called <s>samāsokti</s> because of its condensed expression. For example —
'Praiseworthy is the endurance of the <s>karīra</s> bush in the desert, which has relieved the weariness of travelers;
shame on the splendor of the wish-fulfilling trees on <s>Meru</s>, which fail to serve those in need!'
To show the distinction between <s>samāsokti</s> and <s>aprastuta-praśaṃsā</s> (praise of the irrelevant), he says —
<s>Aprastuta-praśaṃsā</s> (praise of the irrelevant) is [the placement of a parallel subject] when the <s>upameya</s> is only slightly indicated. // VKal_4,3.4 //
When the <s>upameya</s> is indicated by merely a slight hint, and a parallel subject is placed, it is <s>aprastuta-praśaṃsā</s>. For example —

children.text:
lāvaṇyasinduraparaiva hi kācaneyaṃ
  yatrotpalāni śaśinā saha saṃplavante /
  unmañjati dviradakumbhataṭī ca yatra
  yatrāpare kadalikāṇḍamṛṇāladaṇḍāḥ //
children.translated_text: 'This is verily another ocean of beauty's nectar, where lotuses float along with the moon, where the temples of elephants emerge, and where stalks of plantain and lotus-stems [abound].'
The praise of an irrelevant subject constitutes <s>aprastuta-praśaṃsā</s>. //4//
To show that <s>apahṇuti</s> (denial) too is different from these, he says —
<s>Apahṇuti</s> (denial) is the denial of one thing by means of an equivalent thing. // VKal_4,3.5 //

children.text: sanena tulyena vastunā vākyārthenānyasya vākyārthasyāpalāpo nihnavo yastattvādhyāropaṇāyāsāvapahnutiḥ / yathā ----
children.translated_text: The denial — concealment — of one sentence-meaning by another sentence-meaning that is equivalent, for the purpose of superimposing [a different] reality — that is <s>apahṇuti</s>. For example —

children.text: na ketakīnāṃ vilasanti sūcayaḥ pravāsino hanta hasatyayaṃ vidhiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'It is not the spikes of <s>ketakī</s> flowers that gleam — alas, fate mocks the one who is away from home!

children.text: taḍillateyaṃ na cakāsti cañcalā puraḥ smarajyotiridaṃ vivartate //
children.translated_text: It is not a flickering lightning-streak that shines — this is the light of the Love-god manifesting itself.'
Because there is an identity of the two sentence-meanings through the purport, it is not <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor). //5//
Then what is <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) like? He says —
<s>Rūpaka</s> (metaphor) is the superimposition of identity upon the <s>upameya</s> by the <s>upamāna</s>, due to similarity of qualities. // VKal_4,3.6 //

children.text: upamānenopameyasya guṇasāmyāttattvasyābhedasyāropaṇamāropo rūpakam / upamānopameyayorubhayorapi grahaṇaṃ laukikyāḥ kalpitāyāścopamāyāḥ prakṛkṣitvamatra yathā vijñāyeteti / yathā (Uttararāmacarita_1.39) ----
children.translated_text: <s>Rūpaka</s> is the superimposition — the imposition of identity, i.e., non-difference — upon the <s>upameya</s> (object of comparison) by the <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison), due to similarity of qualities. Both <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> are mentioned so that the excellence of both conventional and imagined simile may be understood here. For example (<s>Uttararāmacarita</s> 1.39) —

children.text:
iyaṃ gehe lakṣmīriyamamṛtavartirnayanayo-
  rasāvasyāḥ sparśo vapuṣi vahulaścandanarasaḥ /
  ayaṃ kaṣṭhe vāhuḥ śiśiramasṛṇo mauktikasaraḥ
  kimasyā na preyo paramasahyastu virahaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'She is the <s>Lakṣmī</s> of the house, she is the immortal wick of [my] eyes; her touch on the body is abundant sandalwood-paste; this arm on the shoulder is a cool, smooth string of pearls — what is not dear in her? But separation is supremely unbearable!'

children.text: mukhacandrādīnāṃ tūpamā / samāsānna candrādīnāṃ rūpakatvaṃ yuktamiti //6//
children.translated_text: But '<s>mukhacandra</s>' (moon-face) and the like are [merely] simile. It is not appropriate to consider '<s>candra</s>' and the like as metaphors due to the compound form. //6//
To show the distinction between <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) and <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia), he says —
<s>Śleṣa</s> (paronomasia) is [the superimposition] upon qualities [and other properties], when expressed jointly. // VKal_4,3.7 //

children.text: upamānenopameyasya dharmeṣu guṇakriyāśabdarūpeṣu sa tattvāropaḥ / tantraprayoge tantreṇoccāraṇe sati śleṣaḥ / yathā ----
children.translated_text: The superimposition of identity of the <s>upamāna</s> upon the <s>upameya</s>, with respect to qualities — i.e., properties, actions, and verbal forms — when there is joint expression, i.e., a single utterance, that is <s>śleṣa</s>. For example —

children.text:
ākṛṣṭāmalamaṇḍalāgrarucayaḥ saṃnaddhakṣaḥsthalāḥ
  soṣmāṇo vraṇitā vipakṣahṛdayapronmāthinaḥ karkaśaḥ /
  udvṛttā guravaśca yasya śaminaḥ śyāmāyamānānanā
  yodhā vāravadhūstanāśca na daduḥ kṣobhaṃ sa vo'vyājjinaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Those whose luster at the tips of their stainless circles has been drawn forth, whose chests are bound firm, who are heated, wounded, who agitate the hearts of foes, who are harsh, who are prominent and weighty, who are tranquil yet dark-faced — his warriors and the breasts of courtesans caused him no disturbance, that guileless conqueror — may he protect you!'

children.text: yathā ca gauṇasyārthasyālaṅkāratvaṃ tathā lākṣaṇikasyāpīti darśayitumāha ----
children.translated_text: To show that, just as a secondary (figurative) meaning serves as a figure of speech, so too does a meaning based on <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication), he says —
<s>Vakrokti</s> (oblique expression) consists of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication) based on resemblance. // VKal_4,3.8 //

children.text: bahuni hi nibandhanāni lakṣaṇāyām / tatra sādṛśyāllakṣaṇāvakroktirasāviti / yathā ----
children.translated_text: There are indeed many bases for <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication). Among those, <s>lakṣaṇā</s> based on resemblance is <s>vakrokti</s> (oblique expression). For example —

children.text: unmimīla kamalaṃ sarasīnāṃ kairavaṃ ca na mimīla muhūrtāt /
children.translated_text: 'The lotus of the ponds opened; the water-lily did not close even for a moment.'
Here, opening and closing, which are properties of the eye, indicate blooming and contraction through resemblance.

children.text: iha ca nirantaranavamukulapulakitā harati mādhavī hṛdayam /
children.translated_text: 'The <s>mādhavī</s> creeper, perpetually bristling with fresh buds, captures the heart,
and the breath of the <s>kesara</s> flowers, fragrant with ripened honey, intoxicates.'
Here, 'breath' indicates the emission of fragrance.

children.text:
saṃsthānena sphuratu subhagaḥ svarciṣā cumbatu dyām /
  ālasyamāliṅgati gātramasyāḥ /
  parimlānacchāyāmanuvadati dṛṣṭiḥ kamalinīm /
  pratyūṣeṣu sphuṭitakamalāmodamaitrīkapāyaḥ /
  ūrudvandvaṃ taruṇakadalīkāṇḍasabrahmacāri /
children.translated_text: 'Let it shine forth beautifully in form, let it kiss the sky with its own radiance; laziness embraces her limbs; the gaze imitates the withered hue of the lotus; in the mornings, having abandoned friendship with the fragrance of blooming lotuses; the pair of thighs, fellow brahmacārins with the stalks of young plantains' —

children.text: ityevamādiṣu lakṣaṇārtho nirūpyata iti lakṣaṇāyā jhaṭityarthapratipattikṣamatvaṃ rahasyamācakṣata iti /
children.translated_text: in such and similar cases, the meaning through <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication) is to be determined; thus the secret of <s>lakṣaṇā</s> is its capacity for immediate apprehension of meaning.

children.text: asādṛśyanibandhanā tu lakṣaṇā na vakroktiḥ / yathā ----
children.translated_text: But <s>lakṣaṇā</s> not based on resemblance is not <s>vakrokti</s> (oblique expression). For example —
'With the bees, pale as the cut of an old lotus-stalk.'

children.text: atra cchedaḥ sāmīpyād dravyaṃ lakṣayati / tasyaiva gauratvopapatteḥ //8//
children.translated_text: Here, 'cut' indicates the substance through proximity. For paleness can apply to [the cut surface] itself. //8//
To show the distinction of <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) from <s>rūpaka</s> and <s>vakrokti</s>, he says —
<s>Utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) is the imaginative determination of what is not of that nature as being of another nature, for the purpose of exaggeration. // VKal_4,3.9 //

children.text: atadrūpasyātatsvabhāvasya / anyathā atatsvabhāvatayā / adhyavasānamadhyavasāyaḥ / na punaradhyāropo lakṣaṇā vā / atiśayārthamiti bhrāntijñānanivṛttyartham / sādṛśyādiyamutprekṣeti / enāṃ cevādiśabdā dyotayanti / yathā ----
children.translated_text: 'What is not of that nature' means what is not of that essential character. 'Otherwise' means as if of that other essential character. 'Determination' is a settled conviction — not superimposition, nor <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication). 'For the purpose of exaggeration' is stated to exclude illusory knowledge. 'This is <s>utprekṣā</s> based on resemblance' — and the particles '<s>iva</s>' (as if) and the like indicate it. For example —

children.text:
sa vaḥ pāyādindurnavavisalatākoṭikuṭilaḥ
  smarāreryo mūrdhni jvalanakapiṣe bhāti nihitaḥ /
  sravanmandākinyāḥ pratidivasasiktena payasā
  kapālenonmuktaḥ sphaṭikadhavalenāṅkura iva //
children.translated_text: 'May that moon protect you, curved like the tip of a fresh, spreading vine, placed on the head of the enemy of <s>Smara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), upon a skull reddened by fire — like a sprout, white as crystal, watered daily by the flowing waters of the celestial <s>Gaṅgā</s>, released from the skull!'
Some say <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) is the same as <s>utprekṣā</s>. To refute that, he says —
<s>Atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole) is the imaginative ascription of a possible quality or its heightening. // VKal_4,3.10 //

children.text: saṃbhāvyasya dharmasya tadutkarṣasya ca kalpanātiśayoktiḥ / yathā ----
children.translated_text: <s>Atiśayokti</s> is the imaginative ascription of a possible property and its heightening. For example —
'If the waters of the celestial <s>Gaṅgā</s> had two separate streams in the sky,
his chest, dark as a <s>tamāla</s> tree and strung with a pearl-vine, could be compared to it.'
Or for example —

children.text:
malayajarasaviliptatanunavahāralatāvibhūṣitāḥ
  sitataradantapatrakṛtavaktraruco rucirāmalāṃśukāḥ /
  śaśabhṛti vitatadhāmni dhvalayati dharāmavibhāvyatāṃ gatāḥ
  priyavasatiṃ prayānti sukhameva nirastabhiyo'bhisārikāḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Their bodies anointed with sandalwood paste, adorned with fresh pearl-garlands, their faces beautified with bright white tooth-leaves, wearing spotless garments — when the moon spreads its radiance, they become invisible on the earth, the fearless <s>abhisārikās</s> (women going to meet their lovers) proceed happily to the dwelling of the beloved.'

children.text: yathā bhrāntijñānasyarūpotprekṣā tathā saṃśayajñānasvarūpaḥ saṃdeho'pīti darśayitumāha ----
children.translated_text: To show that, just as <s>utprekṣā</s> has the form of illusory knowledge, so too doubt has the form of uncertain knowledge, he says —
<s>Saṃdeha</s> (doubt) is the [deliberate] confusion between <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s>. // VKal_4,3.11 //

children.text: upamānopameyayoratiśayārthaṃ yaḥ kriyate saṃśayaḥ sa saṃdehaḥ / yathā ----
children.translated_text: The doubt that is created between <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison) and <s>upameya</s> (object of comparison) for the purpose of exaggeration is <s>saṃdeha</s>. For example —
'Is this an ear-lotus or an eye?' — O graceful one,

children.text: na niścinoti hṛdayaṃ kintu dolāyate manaḥ //
children.translated_text: the heart cannot decide; indeed, the mind swings like a pendulum.
Like doubt, <s>virodha</s> (apparent contradiction) too is relevant [as a figure]. He says —
<s>Virodha</s> (apparent contradiction) is the semblance of contradiction. // VKal_4,3.12 //
The appearance of something as if contradictory is <s>virodha</s>. For example —

children.text:
pītaṃ pānamidaṃ tvayādya dayite mattaṃ mamedaṃ manaḥ
  patrālī tava kuṅkumena racitā raktā vayaṃ mānini ! /
  tvaṃ tuṅgastanabhāramantharagatirgātreṣu me vepathu-
  stvanmadhye tanutā mamādhṛtiraho premṇo vicitrā gatiḥ //
children.translated_text: 'This drink was drunk by you today, O beloved, yet my mind is the intoxicated one; your cheek-leaf was decorated with <s>kuṅkuma</s>, yet we are the ones who are reddened, O proud one! You are slow-gaited from the weight of your high breasts, yet the trembling is in my limbs; your waist is slender, yet the lack of composure is mine — ah, wondrous is the way of love!'
Or (<s>Amaru</s> 34) —

children.text:
sā bālā vayamapragalbhavacasaḥ sā strī vayaṃ kātarāḥ
  sā pīnonnatimatpayodharayugaṃ dhatte sakhedā vayam /
  sākrāntā jaghanasthalena guruṇā gantuṃ na śaktā vayaṃ
  doṣairanyajanāśritairapaṭavo jātāḥ sma ityadbhutam //
children.translated_text: 'She is a young girl, yet our speech falters; she is a woman, yet we are the timid ones; she bears a pair of full, high breasts, yet we are the distressed ones; she is impeded by her heavy hips and cannot walk, yet we — made incompetent by faults residing in another — this is astonishing!'
To show the distinction of <s>vibhāvanā</s> (causeless effect) from <s>virodha</s>, he says —
<s>Vibhāvanā</s> (causeless effect) is the manifestation of a well-known result despite the negation of its cause. // VKal_4,3.13 //

children.text: kriyāyāḥ pratiṣedhe tasyā eva kriyāyāḥ phalasya prasiddhasya vyaktivibhāvanā / yathā ----
children.translated_text: When an action is negated, yet the well-known result of that very action is manifest — that is <s>vibhāvanā</s>. For example —
'Even in the company of wicked people, corruption does not dwell
in the hearts of the wise, which are pure without being washed.'
In connection with contradiction, he shows <s>ananvaya</s> (self-comparison). He says —
<s>Ananvaya</s> (self-comparison) is when one and the same thing serves as both <s>upameya</s> and <s>upamāna</s>. // VKal_4,3.14 //
When a single entity serves as both the object of comparison and the standard of comparison, that is <s>ananvaya</s>. For example (<s>Hanumānnāṭaka</s> 14.18) —
'The sky is sky-like; the ocean resembles [only] the ocean;
the battle of <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Rāvaṇa</s> is like [the battle of] <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.'
By this, the incomparability [of each thing] is conveyed. //14//
<s>Upameyopamā</s> (reciprocal simile) is [a comparison] in sequence. // VKal_4,3.15 //
When a single entity serves as both <s>upameya</s> and <s>upamāna</s> in alternating sequence, that is <s>upameyopamā</s>. For example —

children.text: khamiva jalaṃ jalamiva khaṃ haṃsa iva śaśī śaśīva haṃso'yam /
children.translated_text: 'The sky is like water, water is like the sky; the <s>haṃsa</s> (swan) is like the moon, the moon is like this <s>haṃsa</s>;
the stars are in the form of <s>kumuda</s> (water-lilies), and the <s>kumudas</s> are in the form of stars.'
Some say this is itself <s>parivṛtti</s> (exchange). To refute that, he says —
<s>Parivṛtti</s> (exchange) is the interchange of properties by similar and dissimilar [things]. // VKal_4,3.16 //

children.text: samena visadṛśena vārthena arthasya parivartanaṃ parivṛttiḥ / yathā ----
children.translated_text: The interchange of a property with another — by means of a similar or dissimilar thing — is <s>parivṛtti</s>. For example —
'Taking the ear-leaf, she offers to him her reddened foot;
because of the exchange of similar things between the two, I think neither is cheated.'
Or —
'Having renounced her necklace, firm in her unshakable resolve, with unsteady glances, her sandalwood-paste wiped off,
she tied on bark-garments, of the hue of the early dawn, their construction torn apart by the protuberance of her breasts.'
To show that the sequence in <s>upameyopamā</s> (reciprocal simile) is different, he says —
The sequence is the sequential connection of <s>upameya</s> and <s>upamāna</s>. // VKal_4,3.17 //

children.text: upameyānāmupamānānāṃ coddeśināmanuddeśināṃ ca kramasambandhaḥ kramaḥ / yathā ----
children.translated_text: The sequential connection (<s>krama</s>) is the correspondence between the objects of comparison and the standards of comparison, between those enumerated and those subsequently specified. As for example —
By the graces of her continuous play, her speech, smile, and glances,
The <s>vallakī</s> (lute), the <s>kunda</s> flower, the jasmine blossom, and the blue lotus garland are surpassed.
In connection with the discussion of sequential correspondence, in order to demonstrate <s>dīpaka</s> (illumination), he says —
<s>Dīpaka</s> (illumination) is a single action [predicated] in sentences expressing both the standard and the object of comparison. // VKal_4,3.18 //

children.text: upamānavākyepūpameyavācyeṣu caikā kriyā anupaṅgataḥ sambandhyamānā dīpakam //18//
children.translated_text: <s>Dīpaka</s> (illumination) is when a single action, connected without restriction, is predicated in sentences expressing the standard and the object of comparison. // 18 //
It is of three kinds, due to the distinction of the action occurring at the beginning, middle, or end of the sentence. // VKal_4,3.19 //

children.text: tat trividhaṃ bhavati / ādimadhyānteṣu vākyeṣu vṛtterbhedāt / yathā ----
children.translated_text: It is of three kinds, due to the distinction of the action occurring at the beginning, middle, or end of the sentences. As for example —

Pleasure-groves are adorned by young blossoms; women by their amorous sports, rich with the intoxication of spring; <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> by the performance of rites prescribed in the <s>Vedas</s>; kings by their valor that has dispersed the enemies.

children.text: brahmāṇaḥ śrutigaditaiḥ kriyākalāpai , rājāno viralitavairibhiḥ pratāpaiḥ //

children.translated_text: The tears of the wives of travelers, and the water of the rain-clouds,
Flow copiously now — there is preparation for the march of armies by the kings.

children.text:
guruśuśrūṣayā vidyā madhugoṣṭhyā manobhavaḥ /
  udayena śaśāṅkasya payodhirabhivardhate //
children.translated_text: By service to the <s>guru</s>, learning [grows]; by sweet conversation, love; by the rising of the moon, the ocean swells.
Just as <s>dīpaka</s>, <s>nidarśana</s> (demonstration) too is concise — thus he says —
<s>Nidarśana</s> (demonstration) is the indication, through the action itself, of the connection between itself and its purpose. // VKal_4,3.20 //

children.text: kriyayaiva śuddhayā svasyātmanastadarthaḥ cānvayasya saṃbandhasya khyāpanaṃ saṃlulitahetudṛṣṭāntavibhāgadarśanānnidarśanam / yathā ----
children.translated_text: <s>Nidarśana</s> (demonstration) is the indication, through the mere action alone, of the connection between itself and its purpose, by demonstrating a blended unity of cause and illustration. As for example —
Sitting too high leads to a fall — thus it proclaims to the wealthy.
A leaf falls when it turns pale — this is the bond between the two, unexpressed in words.

children.text: patatīti kriyā / tasyāḥ svaṃ patanam / tadarthe'tyuccayadādhyāsaḥ patanāyeti śaṃsanam / tasya khyāyanamarthaśālināṃ śaṃsaditi //20//
children.translated_text: 'Falls' is the action. Its own [aspect] is the falling. Its purpose is the proclamation that 'sitting too high leads to a fall.' The indication of that is the proclamation to the wealthy. // 20 //
And this is not <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> (corroboration). For that is of a different nature — thus he explains —
<s>Arthāntaranyāsa</s> (corroboration) is the adduction of another factual meaning for the establishment of what has been stated. // VKal_4,3.21 //

children.text: uktasiddhyai uktasyārthasya siddhyartha vastuno vākyārthāntarasyaiva nyasanamarthāntaranyāsaḥ / vastugrahaṇādarthasya hetornyasanannārthāntaranyāsaḥ / yathā ----

children.translated_text: There is a lake not very far from here, [as known] from the fragrance of lotuses.

children.text: iti / arthāntarasyaiveti vacanam , yatra heturvyāptigūḍhatvāt kathañcit pratīyate tatra yathā syāt / yadyat kṛtakaṃ tattadanityamityevamprāyeṣu māṃ bhūditi / udāharaṇam /
children.translated_text: The phrase 'of another meaning indeed' is stated so that where the reason is somehow perceived [only] because the pervasion is hidden, it should apply. [This is to avoid cases] like 'whatever is produced is impermanent' and the like. Example —

<s>Arthāntaranyāsa</s> (corroboration) is the adduction of another factual meaning — a sentence-meaning different [from the original] — for the establishment of what has been stated. Because of the word 'fact,' the adduction of a reason alone is not <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s>. As for example —
The full-breasted woman, in the presence of her rival, did not cast off from her chest the garland placed there by her beloved,

children.text: srajaṃ na kācidvijahau jalāvilāṃ vasanti hi premṇi guṇā na vastuni //
children.translated_text: Even though it was wet with tears — for virtues reside in love, not in the object.

children.text: arthāntaranyāsasya heturūpatvād , hetoścānvayavyatirekātmakatvānna pṛthagvyatireka iti kecit / tannirāsāthamāha ----
children.translated_text: Some hold that since <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> has the nature of a reason, and since a reason is of the nature of positive and negative concomitance, <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast) is not separate. To refute that, he says —
<s>Vyatireka</s> (contrast) is the superiority of qualities of the object of comparison [over the standard]. // VKal_4,3.22 //

children.text: upameyasya guṇātirekatvaṃ guṇādhikyaṃ yad arthādupamānāt sa vyatirekaḥ / yathā ----
children.translated_text: <s>Vyatireka</s> (contrast) is the superiority — that is, the excess — of qualities of the object of comparison, implicitly over the standard of comparison. As for example —
Truly, the face of the doe-eyed woman is serene and beautiful,
Equal to the moon — but that [moon] is marred by its blemish.
However, some [define it as] an implied quality of the standard not [shared by the subject], constituting <s>vyatireka</s>. As for example —

children.text:
kuvalayavanaṃ pratyākhyātaṃ navaṃ madhu ninditaṃ
  hasitamamṛtaṃ bhagnaṃ svādoḥ padaṃ rasasaṃvadaḥ /
  viṣamupahitaṃ cintāvyājānmanasyapi kāmināṃ
  caturalalitairlīlātantraistavārdhavilokitaiḥ //
children.translated_text: The grove of blue lotuses is rejected, fresh honey is scorned, nectar is laughed at, the domain of taste is shattered in debate — poison is applied even to the minds of lovers under the pretense of thought — by the artful, charming play of your half-glance.
In order to show the distinction of <s>viśeṣokti</s> (specific statement) from <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast), he says —
<s>Viśeṣokti</s> (specific statement) is the strengthening of similarity through the imagined loss of a single quality. // VKal_4,3.23 //

children.text: ekasya guṇasya hāneḥ kalpanāyāṃ śeṣairguṇaissāmyaṃ yattasya dārḍhyaṃ viśeṣoktiḥ / rūpakaṃ cedaṃ prāyeṇeti / yathā (kumāra. 1-10) ----
