children.translated_text: <s>Viśeṣokti</s> (specific statement) is the strengthening of the similarity with the remaining qualities through the imagined loss of a single quality. And this is generally in the form of <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor). As for example (<s>Kumārasaṃbhava</s> 1.10) —
Where the lamps of love-play are not supplied with oil — the <s>Sandhyā</s> twilight is their wick.
Gambling is verily a man's throne — [i.e.,] kingdom without a throne.
(<s>Mṛcchakaṭikā</s> Act 2)
Sleep is a <s>Lakṣmī</s> (fortune) without a lotus.
An elephant is indeed a mobile fortress.
Thus.
Here too, since the word 'mobile' (<s>jaṅgama</s>) implies the removal of the quality of immobility, this is indeed the imagined loss of a single quality. By this [principle] —
A courtesan is verily deceit in bodily form.
Addiction is death with the breath still remaining.
A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is <s>Bṛhaspati</s> on earth.
And so forth — in all such cases, the imagined loss of a single quality has been explained. // 23 //
In order to show <s>vyājastuti</s> (ironic praise) as distinct from <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast) and <s>viśeṣokti</s> (specific statement), he says —
<s>Vyājastuti</s> (ironic praise) is praise [conveyed] through the meaning of censure, by reason of not performing an action expected of someone distinguished. // VKal_4,3.24 //

children.text: atyantaguṇādhiko viśiṣṭastasya ca karma viśiṣṭakarma , tasya sambhāvyasya kartuṃ śakyasyākaraṇānnindāviśiṣṭasāmyasampādanena stotrārthā vyājastutiḥ / yathā ----
children.translated_text: <s>Vyājastuti</s> (ironic praise) has the purpose of praise through establishing similarity with a distinguished [figure] via censure, by reason of the non-performance of an action that the exceedingly superior, distinguished one is expected to perform. As for example —
He built a bridge over the mountain-range, he split seven palm trees with a single arrow,

children.text: evaṃvidhaṃ karma tatāna rāmastvayā kṛtaṃ tanna mudhaiva garvaḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> performed such a deed — what you have done is not that, so your pride is in vain.
In order to show <s>vyājakti</s> (disguised speech) as distinct from <s>vyājastuti</s> (ironic praise), he says —
<s>Vyājakti</s> (disguised speech) is the resemblance of a pretense to the truth. // VKal_4,3.25 //

children.text: vyājasya cchadmanaḥ satyena sārūpyaṃ vyājoktiḥ / yāṃ māyoktirityāhuḥ / yathā ----
children.translated_text: <s>Vyājakti</s> (disguised speech) is the resemblance of a pretense — a concealment — to the truth. This is what [others] call <s>māyokti</s> (deceptive speech). As for example —
O beautiful one, this tearful face of yours has been made [to look so]
By a fragment of <s>kāśa</s> grass blossom, pale as an autumn moon, blown by the wind.
He states <s>tulyayogitā</s> (co-application) as separate from <s>vyājastuti</s> (ironic praise) —
<s>Tulyayogitā</s> (co-application) is the conjunction in a single simultaneous action with a distinguished [being] for the purpose of showing equality. // VKal_4,3.26 //

children.text: viśiṣṭena nyūnasya sāmyarthamekakālāyāṃ kriyāyāṃ yogastulyayogitā / yathā ----
children.translated_text: <s>Tulyayogitā</s> (co-application) is the conjunction of the lesser with the distinguished in a simultaneous action for the purpose of showing equality. As for example —
The serpent-lord bears this earth girdled by the ocean, and so does your arm.
<s>Ākṣepa</s> (censure) is the rejection of the standard of comparison. // VKal_4,3.27 //

children.text: upamānasya kṣepaḥ pratiṣedha upamānākṣepaḥ / tulyakāryārthasya nairarthakyavivakṣāyām / yathā ----
children.translated_text: <s>Upamānākṣepa</s> (rejection of the standard) is the negation of the standard of comparison, when it is desired to express the purposelessness of something with an equivalent function. As for example —

children.text:
tasyāścenmukhamasti saumyasubhagaṃ kiṃ pārvaṇenendunā
  saundaryasya padaṃ dṛśau ca yadi cet kiṃ nāma nīlotpalaiḥ /
  kiṃ vā komalakāntibhiḥ kisalayaiḥ satyeva tatrādhare
  hā dhātuḥ punaruktavasturacanārambheṣvapūrvo grahaḥ //
children.translated_text: If her face, serene and beautiful, exists, what need is there of the full moon? If those eyes are the abode of beauty, what need of blue lotuses? What need of tender sprouts when such a lower lip exists? Alas, the Creator has a strange fondness for redundant creations!
The meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is also: the apprehension [of the subject] through the rejection of the standard. As for example —
<s>Indra's</s> bow, with a cloud made pale, bearing the appearance of a moist scratch-mark, the autumn
Reconciling the blemished moon, produced a heat greater than the sun's.

children.text: atra śaradveśyeva , induṃ nāyakamiva , raveḥ pratināyakasyevetyupamānāni ganyanta iti //27//
children.translated_text: Here, autumn is understood as if a courtesan, the moon as if the hero, and the sun as if the rival — these are the standards of comparison. // 27 //
He states the distinction of <s>sahokti</s> (co-statement) from <s>tulyayogitā</s> (co-application) —
<s>Sahokti</s> (co-statement) is the expression in a single word of two things and actions that occur simultaneously. // VKal_4,3.28 //

children.text: vastudvasya kriyayostulyakālayorekena padenābhidhānaṃ sahārthaśabdasāmarthyāt sahoktiḥ / yathā ----
children.translated_text: <s>Sahokti</s> (co-statement) is the expression in a single word of two things and their simultaneous actions, through the force of the word 'saha' (together). As for example —

children.text: astaṃ bhāsvān prayātaḥ saha ripubhirayaṃ saṃhriyantāṃ balāni /
children.translated_text: The sun has set together with the enemies — let the armies be withdrawn!

children.text: atrārthayornyūnatvaviśiṣṭatve na sta iti neyaṃ tulyayogiteti //
children.translated_text: Here, since there is no [relation of] inferiority or distinction between the two meanings, this is not <s>tulyayogitā</s>.
One collected [figure] remains. To state its definition —
<s>Samāhita</s> (identification) is the identification with that to which the resemblance is perceived. // VKal_4,3.29 //

children.text: yasya vastunaḥ sādṛśyaṃ gṛhyate tasya vastunaḥ sampattiḥ samāhitam / yathā ----
children.translated_text: <s>Samāhita</s> (identification) is the identification with the thing to which the resemblance of another thing is perceived. As for example —

children.text:
tanvī Meghajalārdravalkalatayā dhautādharevāśrubhiḥ
  śūnyevābharaṇaiḥ svakālavirahādviśrāntapuṣpodgamā /
  cintāmohamivāsthitā madhulihāṃ śabdairvinā lakṣyate
  caṇḍī māmavadhūya pādapatitaṃ jātānutāpeva sā //
children.translated_text: Slender, as if wearing a garment of moist cloud-water bark, with her lower lip washed by tears, as if devoid of ornaments, her blossoming ceased from the separation of her season, standing as if in the stupor of anxiety, seen without the sound of bees — that <s>Caṇḍī</s> creeper, as if having rejected me who fell at her feet, appears as if filled with remorse.

children.text: atra purūravaso latāyāmurvaśyāḥ sādṛśyaṃ gṛhṇataḥ saiva latorvaśī saṃpanneti //29//
children.translated_text: Here, as <s>Purūravas</s> perceives in the creeper the resemblance of <s>Urvaśī</s>, that very creeper has become <s>Urvaśī</s>. // 29 //

children.text: ete cālaṅkārāḥ śuddhā miśrāśca prayoktavyā iti viśiṣṭānām alaṅkārāṇāṃ miśratvaṃ saṃsṛṣṭirityāha ----
children.translated_text: These ornaments are to be employed both pure and mixed — to indicate the mixture of distinguished ornaments, he speaks of <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (combination) —
<s>Saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (combination) is when one ornament becomes the source of another ornament. // VKal_4,3.30 //

children.text: alaṅkārasyālaṅkārayonitvaṃ yadasau saṃsṛṣṭiriti / saṃsargaḥ sambandha iti //30//
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (combination) is when one ornament becomes the source of another. <s>Saṃsarga</s> means connection. // 30 //
Its two divisions are <s>upamā-rūpaka</s> (simile-metaphor) and <s>utprekṣā-avayava</s> (fancy-component). // VKal_4,3.31 //
The two divisions of that combination are <s>upamā-rūpaka</s> (simile-metaphor) and <s>utprekṣā-avayava</s> (fancy-component). // 31 //
<s>Upamā-rūpaka</s> is a metaphor born of simile. // VKal_4,3.32 //
This is clear. As for example —

children.text: niravadhi ca nirāśrayaṃ ca yasya sthitamanivartitakautukaprapañcam /
children.translated_text: Whose boundless and unsupported [glory] stands with the display of inexhaustible wonder,

children.text: prathama iva bhavān sa kūrmamūrtirjayati caturdaśalokavallikandaḥ //
children.translated_text: Like you, that first one in the <s>Kūrma</s> (tortoise) form is victorious — the root-bulb of the creeper of the fourteen worlds!
The moon is the <s>tilaka</s> mark of night, the wife of <s>Lodhra</s> —
And such examples of its varieties should be observed. // 32 //
Similarly —
<s>Utprekṣā-avayava</s> (fancy-component) is the reason for an <s>utprekṣā</s> (fancy). // VKal_4,3.33 //

children.text: utprekṣāyā heturutprekṣāvayavaḥ / avayavaśabdo hyārambhakaṃ lakṣayati / yathā ----
children.translated_text: <s>Utprekṣā-avayava</s> is the reason for the <s>utprekṣā</s> (fancy). The word '<s>avayava</s>' (component) denotes what initiates [it]. As for example —
Grasping the mass of hair as if with fingers, restraining darkness with its rays,
The moon, having made the lotuses close their eyes, kisses as it were the face of the night.
Through these illustrations — one's own and others', in abundance —
This <s>upamā</s> (simile) itself, containing the variety of words, has been elaborated.

children.text:
alaṅkāraikadeśā ye matāḥ saubhāgyabhāginaḥ /
  te'pyalaṅkāradeśīyā yojanīyāḥ kavīśvaraiḥ //
children.translated_text: Those that are considered parts of ornaments, sharing in beauty, should also be employed by master poets as belonging to the category of ornaments.

children.text: iti śrīkāvyālaṅkārasūtravṛttāvālaṅkārike caturthe'dhikaraṇe tṛtīyodhyāyaḥ / samāptaṃ cedamālañkārikaṃ caturthamadhikaraṇam /
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third chapter of the fourth section on ornaments in the <s>Kāvyālaṅkārasūtravṛtti</s>. Thus is completed the fourth section on ornaments.
The first chapter of the fifth section.

children.text: samprati kāvyasamayaṃ śabdaśuddhiṃ ca darśayituṃ prāyogikākhyamadhikaraṇamārabhyate / tatra kāvyasamayastāvaducyate /
children.translated_text: Now, in order to discuss poetic convention and purity of words, the section called 'Practical' (<s>prāyogika</s>) is commenced. Therein, first the poetic conventions are stated.

children.text: naikaṃ padaṃ dviḥ prayojyaṃ prāyeṇa // VKal_5,1.1 //
children.translated_text: Generally, a single word should not be used twice. // VKal_5,1.1 //

children.text: ekaṃ padaṃ na dviḥ prayojyaṃ prāyeṇa bāhulyena / yathā ----

children.translated_text: '<s>payoda-payoda</s>' (cloud-cloud).
However, certain words like '<s>iva</s>' and the like may be used twice. As for example —
'The good are good, the wicked are wicked.'
A single word should not be used twice, generally, that is, predominantly. As for example —
<s>Saṃhitā</s> (euphonic combination) is always [applied] within verse-feet as if within a single word, except at the half-verse boundary. // VKal_5,1.2 //

children.text: nityaṃ saṃhitāpādeṣvekapadavadekasminniva pade / tatra hi nityāsaṃhitetyānnāyaḥ / yathā ----

children.translated_text: <s>Saṃhitā</s> is always [obligatory] within a single word, [and] between verbal roots and prefixes.
Thus. Except at the half-verse boundary — excluding the end of the half-verse. // 2 //

<s>Saṃhitā</s> (euphonic combination) is always applied within verse-feet as if within a single word. For the rule states that '<s>saṃhitā</s> is obligatory within a single word.' For between verbal roots and prefixes, [the rule is] —
The final light [syllable] of a verse-foot should not be [counted as] heavy everywhere. // VKal_5,1.3 //

children.text: pādāntalaghorgurutvaṃ prayoktavyam / na sarvatra , na sarvasmin vṛtta iti / yathā ----
children.translated_text: The [license of counting] the final light syllable of a verse-foot as heavy should be employed — but not everywhere, not in every meter. As for example —

children.text:
yāsāṃ balirbhavati madgṛhadehalīnāṃ
  haṃsaiśca sārasagaṇaiśca viluptapūrvaḥ /
  tāsveva pūrvabalirūḍhayavāṅkurāsu
  bījāñjaliḥ patati kīṭamukhāvalīḍhaḥ //
children.translated_text: The offering at the threshold of my house, previously consumed by geese and flocks of cranes — on those very [thresholds], now with sprouted barley, falls a handful of seeds gnawed by insects.
Only in such meters [is it applied]. But not —
As the dust of the armies spread, the entire world was as if with eyes closed.
And so on. The word 'ca' (and) is for the purpose of carrying over the [phrase] 'except at the half-verse boundary.' // 3 //

children.text: na gādye samāptaprāyaṃ vṛttam, anyatrodgatādibhyaḥ saṃvādāt // VKal_5,1.4 //
children.translated_text: In prose, a nearly complete metrical pattern should not [be used]; in other [cases], because of agreement with <s>udgatā</s> and similar [irregular meters]. // VKal_5,1.4 //

children.text: gadye samāptaprāyaṃ vṛttaṃ na vidheyam / śobhābhrāṃśat / anyatrodgatādibhyo viṣamavṛttebhyaḥ saṃvādād gadyeneti //4//
children.translated_text: In prose, a nearly complete metrical pattern should not be employed, as it diminishes the beauty. In other cases, [it is acceptable] because of agreement with irregular meters like <s>udgatā</s> and others, as [they resemble] prose. //4//
At the beginning of a verse-quarter, [words like] <s>khalu</s> and the like [should not be used]. // VKal_5,1.5 //

children.text: pādādau khalvādayaḥ śabdā na prayojyāḥ / ādiśabdaḥ prakārārthaḥ / yeṣāmādau prayogo na śloṣyati te gṛhyante / na punarvatahetaprabhṛtayaḥ //5//
children.translated_text: At the beginning of a verse-quarter, words like <s>khalu</s> and the like should not be employed. The word 'and the like' indicates a class; those whose use at the beginning is not pleasing are included. But not [words like] <s>vata</s>, <s>hetu</s>, and so forth. //5//
In half [a verse], there should not be a somewhat incomplete sentence. // VKal_5,1.6 //
In a half-verse, a somewhat incomplete sentence should not be employed. For example —
The curved fingertips of <s>Śambhu</s> in his <s>tāṇḍava</s> (cosmic dance) are victorious;
and the hands and arms of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, tawny-hued with the radiance of the discus.
A <s>karmadhāraya</s> (appositional compound) that produces a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> (possessive compound) interpretation [should not be used]. // VKal_5,1.7 //

children.text: bahubrīhipratipattiṃ karoti yaḥ karmadhārayaḥ sa na prayoktavyaḥ / yathā ----
children.translated_text: A <s>karmadhāraya</s> compound that produces a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> interpretation should not be employed. For example —
'perched upon' and 'tree' [forming] '<s>adhyāsitataruḥ</s>' (the one with the perched-upon tree) —
thus. //7//
By this, the reverse is also explained. // VKal_5,1.8 //
A <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound that produces a <s>karmadhāraya</s> interpretation should also not be employed. For example —
'He whose men are heroes' — that is <s>vīrapuruṣaḥ</s> (hero-man);
'He whose cry is melodious' — that is <s>kalaravaḥ</s> (melodious-cry).
Thus. //8//
In the reversal of a supposed negation, two negatives [should be used]. // VKal_5,1.9 //

children.text: sambhāvyasya niṣedhasya nivartane svau pratiṣedhau prayoktavyau yathā ----
children.translated_text: In the reversal of a supposed negation, two negatives should be employed. For example —

children.text: samaramūrdhani yena tarasvinā na na jito vijayī tridaśeśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: By that swift warrior, in the forefront of battle, the victorious lord of the gods was not not conquered;
yet now he, his body smeared with blood from the successive arrows of the ascetic, has taken refuge on the ground.
When the qualified [noun] is already understood, only the qualifier should be used. // VKal_5,1.10 //

children.text: viśeṣyasya pratipattau jātāyāṃ viśeṣaṇamātrasyaiva prayogaḥ / yathā (Raghuvaṃśa 3.9) ----
children.translated_text: When the understanding of the qualified [noun] has arisen, only the qualifier should be employed. As in (<s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> 3.9) —
'As if containing treasures within, with the ocean as her garment' —

children.text: atra hi pṛthivyā viśeṣaṇamātrameva prayuktam / etena
children.translated_text: here, for the earth, only the qualifier has been employed. By this,
'Then from the forehead-slab of that angered ancient enemy of the gods, a lofty light arose;
meanwhile, like lightning from a mountain, <s>Acyuta</s> rose swiftly from his throne with great speed' —
such [examples] are also explained. //10//
A pronoun [serves as] a recall of what is hidden within a compound. // VKal_5,1.11 //

children.text: sarvanāmnānusandhiranusandhānaṃ pratyavamarśaḥ / vṛtticchannasya vṛttau samāse channasya guṇībhūtasya / yathā ----
children.translated_text: A recall through a pronoun means a bringing back to mind — of what is hidden within a compound, that is, of what has become subordinate within a compound formation. For example —
'Of your face too, O you whose eyes are like blue lotus petals, whose fragrance equals that of lotus pollen' —
The genitive case may sometimes [be used] even for a relation of a relation. // VKal_5,1.12 //

children.text: sambandhena sanbandhaḥ sambandhasambandhastasmin ṣaṣṭhī prayojyā kvacit , na sarvatreti / yathā

children.translated_text: 'The root of the lotus' —

children.text: iti / kamalena saṃbaddhā kamalinī tasyā kandaḥ iti sambandhaḥ / tena kadalīkāṇḍādayo vyākhyātāḥ //12//
children.translated_text: thus. The lotus plant is related to the lotus [flower]; 'its root' is the relation. By this, [compounds like] 'the stem of the plantain' and the like are explained. //12//
A relation of a relation means a relation through a relation; in that case, the genitive should sometimes be employed, but not always. For example —
A dialectal word that is extensively used [by poets may be employed]. // VKal_5,1.13 //

children.text: atīva kavibhiḥ prayuktaṃ deśabhāṣāpadaṃ prayojyam / yathā ----

'He desired a woman, not <s>hālā</s> (liquor)' —
here,
'<s>hālā</s>'

children.text: iti deśabhāṣāpadam / anatiprayuktaṃ tu na prayojyam / yathā ----
children.translated_text: is a dialectal word. But one not extensively used should not be employed. For example —
'Making dance the dense, freely shining shoots of the <s>kaṅkelī</s> (a type of creeper) garden row' —
here,
'<s>kaṅkelī</s>'
is [such an inappropriate dialectal] word. //13//
Gender [anomaly] and ellipsis [are acceptable when extensively used]. // VKal_5,1.14 //
Both gender [anomaly] and ellipsis, when extensively used, should be employed. For example —

children.text: vatse ! mā bahu niḥśvasīḥ kuru surāgaṇḍūpamekaṃ śanaiḥ
children.translated_text: 'Dear child, do not sigh so much; slowly take one mouthful (<s>gaṇḍūṣa</s>) of divine nectar' —

children.text: ityādiṣu gaṇḍūṣaśabdaḥ puṃsi bhūyasā prayukto , na striyām āmnāto'pi strītvaṃ / adhyāhāro yathā ----
children.translated_text: in such [examples], the word <s>gaṇḍūṣa</s> is predominantly used in the masculine, not in the feminine, even though [the feminine] is recorded. Ellipsis, for example —

children.text: mā bhavantamanalaḥ pavano vā vāraṇo madakalaḥ paraśurvā /
children.translated_text: 'Let not fire, or wind, or a maddened elephant, or an axe,

children.text: vāhinījalabharaḥ kuliśaṃ vā svasti te'stu latayā saha vṛkṣa ! //

'burned,' 'felled,'
and other [verbs] are to be supplied through ellipsis as required by the syntactic connection. //14//
Here indeed,
Words based on secondary signification [are also acceptable when extensively used]. // VKal_5,1.15 //

children.text: lakṣaṇāśabdāścātiprayuktāḥ prayojyāḥ / yathā dvirepharodaraśabdau bhramaracakravākārthau lakṣaṇāparau / anatiprayuktāśca na prayojyāḥ / yathā ---- dvikaḥ kāka iti //15//
children.translated_text: Words based on secondary signification (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>), when extensively used, should be employed. For example, the words <s>dvirepha</s> (two-r's) and <s>udara</s> (belly), meaning 'bee' and <s>cakravāka</s> respectively, are based on secondary signification. Those not extensively used should not be employed — for example, <s>dvikaḥ</s> meaning 'crow.' //15//
There should not be an abundance of those [secondary-signification words] in a single [sentence]. // VKal_5,1.16 //

children.text: teṣāṃ lakṣaṇāśabdānāṃ bāhulyamekasmin vākye na prayojyam / śakyate hyekasyāvācakasya vācakavadbhāvaḥ kartuṃ , na bahūnāmiti //16//
children.translated_text: An abundance of those words based on secondary signification should not be employed in a single sentence, for it is possible to make one non-denotative word function as if denotative, but not many. //16//
The class-nature of [words like] <s>stana</s> (breast) and the like is generally invested with duality. // VKal_5,1.17 //

children.text: stanādīnāṃ dvitvāviṣṭā dvitvādhyāsitā jātiḥ prāyeṇa bāhulyene ti / yathā ----

children.translated_text: 'The eyes of women' —
thus.
The class-nature of [words like] <s>stana</s> and the like is invested with duality — that is, pervaded by duality — generally, meaning predominantly. For example —

children.text: atha kathaṃ dvitvāviṣṭatvaṃ jāteḥ ? / taddhi dravye , na jātau / atadrūpatvājjāteḥ / na doṣaḥ ; tadatadrūpatvājjāteḥ[k: tadrūpatvājjāteḥ] / kathaṃ tadatadrūpatvaṃ[k: tadrūpatvaṃ] jāteḥ ? / taddhi jaiminīyā jānanti[k: jainā jānānti] / vayaṃ tu lakṣyasiddhau siddhaparamatāmuvādinaḥ / na caivamatiprasaṅgaḥ / lakṣyānusāritvānnyāyasyeti / evamanyāpi vyavasthohyā //17//
children.translated_text: Now, how is the class-nature invested with duality? For duality belongs to the substance, not to the class, since the class is not of that nature. There is no fault; [we say it] because the class is of the nature of that [which possesses it]. How is the class of the nature of that [substance]? The <s>Jaiminīya</s> school knows this. We, however, in matters of established usage, follow the principle of priority of established forms. And there is no excessive extension [of this principle], because the rule follows [actual] usage. Other determinations too should be made similarly. //17//

children.text: iti śrīkāvyālaṅkārasūtravṛttau prāyogike pañcame'dhikaraṇe prathamo'dhyāyaḥ / kāvyasamayaḥ //5-1//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first chapter of the fifth section on practical application, in the <s>Śrī Kāvyālaṅkārasūtravṛtti</s>: on poetic conventions. //5-1//

In the usage '<s>Rudrau</s>' (the two <s>Rudras</s>),

children.text: ityatra prayoge ekaśeṣo7nveṣyo'nveṣaṇīyaḥ / rudraśca rudrāṇī ceti

children.translated_text: 'The collection of verbal roots grows' —

children.text: iti hi śabdavida ācakṣate / tenaiṣāṃ gaṇapāṭho'numataḥ / śiṣṭaprayogāditi //2//
children.translated_text: thus the grammarians state. Therefore, their listing in the <s>gaṇapāṭha</s> is approved, based on the usage of the learned. //2//

Usages like '<s>milati</s>' (meets), '<s>viklavati</s>' (is distressed), '<s>kṣapayati</s>' (destroys), and the like — how is the verbal root status of <s>mili</s>, <s>klabi</s>, <s>kṣapi</s>, and the like [justified]? [Objection:] Because the designation of 'verbal root' is assigned only to those listed in the <s>gaṇapāṭha</s> (root-catalogue). To this he says — because the collection of verbal roots is not closed.

'Swaying, trembling with modesty' —
in such usages without [the expected ātmanepada]. That this is so, he says — from the <s>jñāpaka</s> (indicatory sign). //3//
The <s>ātmanepada</s> of <s>val</s>, arising from the <s>anudātta</s> (grave accent), is seen to be non-invariable —
What then is that indicatory sign? To this he says —

children.translated_text: The double marking of <s>cakṣiṅ</s> [is the indicatory sign]. // VKal_5,2.4 //

children.text:
cakṣiṅ ikāreṇaivānudāttena siddhamātmanepadasyānityatvajñāpanārtham /
[k: siddhātmanepadam ; kimarthaṃ ṅitkaraṇam ? tatkriyate anudāttanimittasyātmanepadasyānityatvajñāpanārtham /]
children.translated_text: [The <s>ātmanepada</s>] is already established for <s>cakṣiṅ</s> by the <s>ī</s>-marker alone with its <s>anudātta</s> accent; the purpose of making it <s>ṅit</s> additionally is to indicate the non-invariability of the <s>ātmanepada</s> caused by the <s>anudātta</s>.

children.text: etena , vedi-bhartsi-tarji-prabhṛtayo vyākhyātāḥ / āvedayati-bhartsayati- tarjayatītyādīnāṃ prayogāṇāṃ darśanāt / anyatrāpyanudāttanibandhanasyātmanepadasyānityatyaṃ jñāpakena draṣṭavyamiti //4//
children.translated_text: By this, <s>vedi</s>, <s>bhartsi</s>, <s>tarji</s>, and the like are explained — since usages like '<s>āvedayati</s>' (informs), '<s>bhartsayati</s>' (threatens), '<s>tarjayati</s>' (menaces), and the like are observed. In other cases too, the non-invariability of the <s>ātmanepada</s> based on the <s>anudātta</s> should be recognized through the <s>jñāpaka</s>. //4//
'<s>Kṣīyate</s>' — this is [to be understood as] the <s>karmakartr</s> (objective-agentive) construction. // VKal_5,2.5 //

children.text: kṣīyatī iti prayogo dṛśyate , sa karmakartari draṣṭavyaḥ / kṣīyateranātmanepaditvāt //5//
children.translated_text: The usage '<s>kṣīyate</s>' (is diminished) is observed; it should be understood in the <s>karmakartr</s> (objective-agentive) construction, because <s>kṣī</s> does not take the <s>ātmanepada</s> [in the active]. //5//
And '<s>khidyate</s>' likewise. // VKal_5,2.6 //

children.text: khidyata iti ca prayogo dṛśyate , so'karmakartaryeva draṣṭavyā , na kartari / adaivādikatvāt khideḥ //6//
children.translated_text: The usage '<s>khidyate</s>' (is depressed) is also observed; it should be understood only in the objective-agentive construction, not in the [simple] active voice, because <s>khid</s> does not belong to the <s>daivādi</s> class. //6//
The <s>ātmanepada</s> of <s>mārg</s> (to seek) is irregular. // VKal_5,2.7 //
'<s>mārga</s>, in the sense of searching' —
is listed.

children.text: iti vikalpitaṇickastasyādyadātmanepadaṃ dṛśyate ---- mārgantāṃ dehabhāramiti , tadalakṣma alakṣaṇam / parasmaipaditvānmārgeḥ / tathā ca śiṣṭaprayogaḥ ----

And the usage of the learned is —
In the <s>curādi</s> class,
'Shaking and shaking her tender sprout-like hand, she searches for her garments.'
'<s>Lolamāna</s>' and the like are [to be understood] without the <s>śānac</s> suffix. // VKal_5,2.8 //

children.text: lolamāno vellamāna ityādayaścānaśi draṣṭavyāḥ / śānacastvabhāvaḥ , parasmaipaditvāddhātūnāmiti //8//
children.translated_text: Forms like '<s>lolamāna</s>' (swaying), '<s>vellamāna</s>' (rolling), and the like should be understood as being without the <s>śānac</s> suffix, because the roots take the <s>parasmaipada</s>. //8//
For <s>labh</s>, when having the sense of motion, in the <s>ṇic</s>-causative, the <s>ṇ</s> and <s>au</s> endings apply when the agent [becomes] the object or does not. // VKal_5,2.9 //

dīrghikāsu kumudāni vikāsaṃ lambhayanti śiśirāḥ śaśibhāsaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'In the ponds, the cool moonbeams cause the water-lilies to bloom.'

There is a [root] <s>labh</s> which denotes motion subsidiary to attainment, and [another] which denotes attainment subsidiary to motion. In the first case, since <s>labh</s> has the sense of motion, in the <s>ṇic</s>-causative, by the <s>gatyādi</s> rule, the agent receives the designation of object. For example —

<s>Acyuta</s> spoke words of pure smiling.' //
The words '<s>te</s>' and '<s>me</s>' are [to be understood as] indeclinables. // VKal_5,2.10 //

'That the <s>Vedas</s> have been studied was not known to me (<s>me</s>) before.'
'<s>Tiraskṛta</s>' in the sense of 'humiliated,' through figurative extension from '<s>antardhā</s>' (concealment). // VKal_5,2.11 //

children.translated_text: is also explained. Here too the compound is as stated above. And this rule applies in usages by the learned. Therefore there is no over-extension. //15//

children.translated_text: A <s>bahuvrīhi</s> [compound] with different case-relations should not be rejected — it should not be avoided. Having <s>janma</s> and such as the latter member. As follows —

— thus.
<s>Hastāgra</s>, <s>agrahasta</s>, and such are due to the distinction or non-distinction of the quality and the qualified. // VKal_5,2.20 [*VKal_5,2.19] //

children.text: hastāgram agrahastaḥ , puṣpāgram , agrapuṣpamityādayaḥ prayogāḥ katham ? āhitāgnyādiṣvapāṭhāt / pāṭhe vā tadaniyamaḥ syāt / āha ---- guṇaguṇinorbhedābhedāt / tatra bhedād , hastāgrādayaḥ / abhedādagrahastādayaḥ //20//

Because they are not listed in the <s>āhitāgni</s> class. Or, if listed, there would be no restriction [on order]. children.text: śakyamiti rūpaṃ karmābhidhāyāṃ liṅgavacanasyāpi sāmānyopakramāt // VKal_5,2.23 [*VKal_5,2.22] //

children.translated_text: (<s>Pāṇini</s> 3.1.99) — when the passive with <s>ya</s> suffix is formed for the object, the form <s>śakyam</s> arises. From the root <s>śak</s> (to be able),

In the <s>sūtra</s> 'by which there is modification of a limb'

children.text: (Pā_2,3.20) ityatra sūtre yathāṅgānāṃ hānistathādhikyamapi vikāraḥ / yathā ----

children.text: mahīdhra-dharaṇīdhrādayaḥ śabdāḥ mūlavibhujādidarśanāt kapratyaye satīti / garhīṃ dharatīti mahīdhra iti / evamādayo'nye'pi draṣṭavyāḥ //34//

children.text: tairvidādibhirhīdharādayo vyākhyātāḥ / dharatīti dharaḥ / mahyā dharo mahīdharaḥ / evaṃ gaṅgādharādayo vyākhyātāḥ //37//

'<s>śubh</s> and <s>śumbh</s> — in the sense of beauty'

children.text: iti śubherbhidāderākṛtigaṇatvādaṅ siddha eva / guṇapratiṣedhābhāvastu nipātyata iti / śobhārthāvityatraikadeśe , kiṃ śobhā , āhosvicchobha iti viśeṣāvagatirācaryaparamparopadeśāditi //41//

(Pā_3,3.103) iti striyāṃ bahulaṃ vivakṣā / kvicidvivakṣā , kvacidavivakṣā , kvacidubhayamiti /
vivakṣā yathā ---- īhā lajjeti / avivakṣā yathā ---- ātaṅka iti / vivakṣāvivakṣe yathā bādhā bādhaḥ , ūhā ūhaḥ , vrīḍā vrīḍaḥ , iti //42//

children.translated_text: In [the form] <s>kṣatadṛḍhoras</s> (with wounded firm chest), <s>kap</s> [suffix] does not apply, because of the prohibition of the <s>tadantavidhi</s>. // VKal_5,2.68 //
"The <s>rākṣasas</s>, with firm chests scratched by the tips of monkey-claws"
from the word <s>dṛḍhoras</s> (firm-chested),

(<s>Pāṇini</s> 5.4.151) — the <s>kap</s> suffix was not applied,
because "by a stem that contains the listed [word]"

— here,

In '<s>apāṅganetra</s>' (side-glanced eye), the <s>luk</s> [elision of the case-ending] is not obtainable. // VKal_5,2.70 //
because by the rule '<s>amūrdhamastakāt svāṅgād akāme</s>'
(<s>Pāṇini</s> 6,3.12), the non-elision (<s>aluk</s>) of the seventh case-ending is prescribed. //70//
'<s>Apāṅge netraṃ yasyāḥ</s>' — she whose eye is at the side-glance — in '<s>apāṅganetrā</s>,' the <s>luk</s> elision is not obtainable,

because the <s>puṃvadbhāva</s> (masculine-like treatment) of women

(<s>Pāṇini</s> 6,3.61): by the prescription of shortening [according to <s>Gālava</s>]. //73//
How are usages like '<s>jambulatā</s>' and the like [justified]? He says: by the rule prescribing shortening.
Words like '<s>tilaka</s>' and the like are to be [found] among the <s>ajirādi</s> group. // VKal_5,2.74 //
in '<s>tilakavatī</s>, <s>kanakavatī</s>'
and the like, when the suffix <s>matup</s> [is added],
by the rule '<s>matau bahvaco'najirādīnām</s>'
(<s>Pāṇini</s> 6,3.119), lengthening would occur. But some explain [it differently] —
the <s>matup</s> [prescribed by] '<s>nadyāṃ matup</s>'

children.text: (Pā_4,2.85) iti yo matup tatrāyaṃ vidhiḥ / teṣāṃ matenāmarāvatītyādīnāmasiddhiḥ //74//
children.translated_text: (<s>Pāṇini</s> 4,2.85) — to that <s>matup</s> this rule applies. By their view, forms like '<s>Amarāvatī</s>' and the like would not be derivable. //74//

The forms '<s>niśamya</s>' and '<s>niśamayya</s>' [differ] due to a difference in the base root. // VKal_5,2.75 //

children.text: niśamya -- niśamayyetyetau śabdau śrutvetyetasminnarthe / śameḥ lyapi

children.text: (Pā_6,4.56) ityayādeśe sati niśamayyeti bhavitavyam , na niśamyeti / āha ---- prakṛtibhedāt / śamerdaivādikasya niśamyeti rūpam /

children.text: iti curādau ṇici mitsaṃjñakasya niśamayyeti rūpam //75//
children.translated_text: from the <s>curādi</s> (10th) class, with the causative <s>ṇic</s> applied to the <s>mit</s>-designated root, the form is '<s>niśamayya</s>.' //75//
'<s>Niśamya</s>' and '<s>niśamayya</s>' — these two words both mean 'having heard.' When the <s>lyap</s> suffix [is applied] to '<s>śam</s>,'
The forms '<s>saṃyamya</s>' and '<s>niyamya</s>' [are correct] because the root does not end in <s>ṇij</s> (causative). // VKal_5,2.76 //
By '<s>lyapi laghupūrvāt</s>'

children.text: (Pā_6,4.56) iti ṇerayādeśena bhavitavyam / āha ---- aṇijantatvāt / dhātorṇic tu na / gatārthatvāt / yathā ----
children.translated_text: (<s>Pāṇini</s> 6,4.56), the <s>ṇer-ay</s>-substitute should apply. He says: because the root does not end in <s>ṇic</s>. The <s>ṇic</s> (causative) is not [applied] to the root, because the meaning is already conveyed. For example —
'<s>Vācaṃ niyacchati</s>' — 'He restrains speech.'

children.text: iti / ṇijarthānayagatau [k: tu] ṇic prayujyata eva / yathā ----
children.translated_text: But where the <s>ṇij</s>-meaning of 'causing another to do' is intended, the <s>ṇic</s> is indeed employed. For example —
'<s>Saṃyamayitum ārabdhaḥ</s>' — 'He began to cause [another] to control.'
How [are justified] the forms '<s>saṃyamya</s>' and '<s>niyamya</s>'?
The form '<s>prapīya</s>' is from the root <s>pīṅ</s>. // VKal_5,2.77 //
is from the root '<s>pīṅ pāne</s>' (to drink).
For from the root '<s>pā</s>' (to drink),
by the rule '<s>na lyapi</s>'
(<s>Pāṇini</s> 6,4.69), the prohibition of the <s>ī</s>-substitute [means] the form would be '<s>prapāya</s>.' //77//
This word '<s>prapīya</s>' (having drunk abundantly)
The form '<s>dūrayati</s>' (makes distant) [is justified] by the word '<s>bahula</s>' (variously) in the rule. // VKal_5,2.78 //
'<s>Dūrayaty avanate vivasvati</s>' — 'It makes distant when the sun descends' —
here, how is the form '<s>dūrayati</s>' [derived]? By the rule for <s>iṣṭhavad</s>-behavior,
'<s>sthūladūra</s>...'

children.text: (Pā_6,4.156) ityādinā guṇalopayoḥ kṛtayordavayatīti bhavitavyam / āha ---- bahulagrahaṇāt /
children.translated_text: (<s>Pāṇini</s> 6,4.156) and the like, when both <s>guṇa</s> and <s>lopa</s> are applied, the form should be '<s>davayati</s>.' He says: because of the word '<s>bahula</s>' (variously) [in the rule].
'<s>Pratipadikād dhātvarthe bahulam iṣṭhavac ca</s>'
(<s>Gaṇapāṭha</s> 203) — because of the word '<s>bahula</s>' therein,
the rule '<s>sthūladūra</s>...'
(<s>Pāṇini</s> 6,4.156) and the like need not always apply. //78//
In forms like '<s>gacchatī</s>' and so on, the augment <s>num</s> is not to be prohibited. // VKal_5,2.79 //

children.text: harati hi vanarājirgacchatī śyāmabhāvamityādiṣu gacchatīprabhṛtiṣu śabdeṣu ,

children.translated_text: by the rule '<s>śap-śyanor nityam</s>'
the <s>num</s> augment cannot be prohibited [i.e., is necessarily applied]. //79//
In '<s>harati hi vanarājir gacchatī śyāmabhāvam</s>' — 'The row of trees indeed assumes a dark hue as it goes' — and the like, in forms beginning with '<s>gacchatī</s>,'
The form '<s>mitreṇa goptrā</s>' (by a protector who is a friend) [is justified] by <s>puṃvadbhāva</s> (masculine-like treatment). // VKal_5,2.80 //
'<s>Mitreṇa goptrā</s>' —
how is this [justified]? The form should be '<s>goptṛṇā</s>,'
by the rule '<s>iko'ci vibhaktau</s>'
(<s>Pāṇini</s> 7,3.73), which prescribes the <s>num</s> augment. He says: by <s>puṃvadbhāva</s>.
'<s>Tṛtīyādiṣu bhāṣitapuṃskaṃ puṃvad Gālavasya</s>'
(<s>Pāṇini</s> 7,1.74) — by masculine-like treatment according to <s>Gālava</s>, the form '<s>goptrā</s>' is obtained. //80//
The form '<s>vetsyasi</s>' (you will know) [is justified] by word-splitting. // VKal_5,2.81 //
'<s>Patitaṃ vetsyasi kṣitau</s>' — 'You will know [it as] fallen on the ground' —

children.text: ityatra vetsyasīti na siddhyati / iṭprasaṅgāt / āha ---- padabhaṅgāt siddhyati / vetsyasīti padaṃ bhajyate ---- vetsi , asi /
children.translated_text: here, the form '<s>vetsyasi</s>' is not directly derivable, because the augment <s>iṭ</s> would be expected. He says: it is derivable by word-splitting. '<s>Vetsyasi</s>' is split into: '<s>vetsi</s>' (you know) and '<s>asi</s>' (you are).
'<s>Asi</s>'
— this particle means 'you.' It is sometimes used as a poetic figure. For example —
'You are a king — you spoke the truth.'

as stated by the original grammarian [<s>Pāṇini</s>], if it is underived [i.e., taken as a primitive form]. //82//

children.translated_text: (<s>Pāṇini</s> 7,3.19), when the <s>aṇ</s> suffix is applied to a word ending in '<s>hṛd</s>,' with <s>vṛddhi</s> in both members, the forms become '<s>sauhārda</s>' and '<s>dauhārda</s>.' //83//

From the words '<s>suhṛdaya</s>' and '<s>durhṛdaya</s>,' when the <s>aṇ</s> suffix is applied by the <s>yuvādi</s> listing, '<s>hṛdaya</s>' becomes '<s>hṛd</s>.' With initial <s>vṛddhi</s>, the forms '<s>sauhṛda</s>' and '<s>daurhṛda</s>' arise. The form '<s>virama</s>' (cease!) [is justified] by irregular citation. // VKal_5,2.84 //
by the rule '<s>nodāttopadeśasya</s>...'

by the rule '<s>upary-adhy-adhasaḥ sāmīpye</s>'

— here,

'<s>Mlāyanty aṅgulisaṅge'pi komalāḥ kusumasrajaḥ</s>' — 'Even at the touch of a finger, delicate flower-garlands wilt' —

and '<s>saṃjñāyām agāt</s>'

In '<s>Indravāhana</s>' (one whose vehicle is <s>Indra</s>), <s>ṇatva</s> (retroflexion of '<s>n</s>') does not apply, because the meaning of '<s>āhita</s>' (placed) is not intended. // VKal_5,2.91 //

here,

the [rule]

children.text: (Pā_8,4.8) iti ṇatvaṃ na bhavati / āhitatvasyāvivakṣitatvāt / svasvāmibhāvamātraṃ hyatra vivakṣitam / tena siddham
children.translated_text: (<s>Pāṇini</s> 8,4.8) — the retroflexion of '<s>n</s>' does not apply, because the meaning of '<s>āhita</s>' (placed) is not intended. Only the simple possessive relationship is intended here. Therefore, the form
